target.title: fix(ui): sync agentSelection when switching sessions across agents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI, switching from one agent's session to another agent's session via the session switcher updates the chat panel correctly, but leaves the left sidebar agent chip/select on the previous agent. Because the chip treats a re-click of the already-selected agent as a no-op, operators cannot return to the previous agent without a full reload or another workaround. The chat pane already syncs `agentSelection` from the session key; the sidebar and shell session-select paths did not.

## Evidence

Runtime before/after on the production selection contract (same `parseAgentSessionKey` + `agentSelection.set` sequence as `selectSession` / `selectChatSession`):

```console
$ node scripts/proof-session-switcher-agent-sync.mjs
BEFORE (setSessionKey only):
  sessionKey=agent:research:work
  agentSelection.selectedId=main
  agentId set called: null
  can re-select previous agent after switch: false

AFTER (sync agentSelection from session key):
  sessionKey=agent:research:work
  agentSelection.selectedId=research
  agentId set called: research
  can re-select previous agent after switch: true

RESULT: PASS — session switch keeps agent chip in sync
```

Source paths that now call `agentSelection.set` when the session key encodes an agent id:

- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-navigation.ts` (`selectSession`, `replaceCurrentSession`)
- `ui/src/app/app-host.ts` (`selectChatSession` used by command palette + UI command navigate/split)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Session switcher / command-palette session selection updated chat `sessionKey` but not `agentSelection.selectedId`, so the agent chip stayed on the previous agent and re-clicking that agent no-oped (issue #109087).
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15, Node v26.5.0, worktree `/tmp/oc-109087` on branch `fix/session-switcher-selected-sync` rebased onto latest `upstream/main`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-109087
  node scripts/proof-session-switcher-agent-sync.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the live node proof script (above under Evidence). Before: selecting `agent:research:work` leaves `selectedId=main` so re-selecting main is a no-op. After: `selectedId=research` and the previous agent can be re-selected.
- **Observed result after fix:** Session switch now updates both gateway session key and agent selection, matching the chat pane `applyActiveSessionBindings` contract so the sidebar chip tracks the active agent.
- **What was not tested:** Full browser Control UI against a live multi-agent gateway (no live WebUI session in this environment). Sidebar/host controller coverage was run locally as a supplement outside this proof section.

## Summary

Closes #109087.

Mirror the chat-pane session-binding path: when a session key is selected, parse the agent id and set `agentSelection` before `gateway.setSessionKey` and navigate. Covers sidebar session rows, replace-current, command palette, and shell UI commands.

target.title: fix(ui): stop local assistant attachments from checking forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing a local assistant attachment in the Control UI could see it remain on `Checking...` indefinitely when the authenticated metadata response stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attachment availability owner now applies a 30-second abort deadline to its metadata request and clears the timer on every terminal path. The existing failure path then marks the attachment unavailable and requests a rerender. Successful responses, media tickets, Gateway routes, and the adjacent managed-image fetch path are unchanged.

## User Impact

Stalled local attachment checks now settle to `Unavailable` instead of leaving the chat UI pinned in `Checking...`. Attachments whose metadata responds normally continue to render through their authenticated media-ticket link.

## Evidence

- Before, on a fixed latest-main snapshot, the real Gateway and Chromium Control UI issued the stalled metadata request without a signal; after more than 35 seconds it had not aborted and the attachment still showed `Checking...`. A normal attachment in the same message returned HTTP 200 and rendered successfully.
- After this change, the same real Gateway/Control UI path supplied an abort signal, aborted the stalled request at exactly 30,000ms, removed `Checking...`, and rendered `Unavailable`. The normal control still returned HTTP 200 and rendered a media-ticket link.

- UI typecheck was not run locally because the validation host's cgroup-v1 environment could not attest the required memory, CPU, and process limits. Hosted CI owns that lane.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

Cyber:

```text

Gateway ready after restart

/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

Sovereign:

target.title: fix(slack): bound one-shot WebClient/write timeouts without Bolt deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`@slack/web-api` defaults `timeout` to `0` (no deadline). One-shot Slack WebClient and write clients could hang forever when Slack stalled. Lookup already defaulted to 30s; web/write did not.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prior tip failed CI for two reasons:

1. **Knip** — public `SLACK_*_TIMEOUT_MS` exports with no production callers
2. **Bolt contamination** — `provider.ts` passes `resolveSlackWebClientOptions()` into `createSlackBoltApp`. A default timeout on that shared resolver gives Bolt's long-lived client a request deadline

**Fix shape (Bolt-safe):**
- `resolveSlackWebClientOptions` stays **timeout-free** (Bolt / Socket Mode)
- `createSlackWebClient` applies a private **30s** one-shot deadline
- `resolveSlackWriteClientOptions` applies a private **60s** write deadline
- No new public timeout constant exports
- Whole-path stalled-header proofs in `client.web-api.test.ts`

## User Impact

- One-shot Slack API calls get bounded timeouts
- Bolt / Socket Mode listener path unchanged

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `e37190fea8c9cd1bcdf41bbc04e42a28c5bd9632`
**Base:** `8bf4d388b05dbce93a449fd8bffc621bd12825a2`

| Check | Result |
|---|---|

target.title: fix(ci): bound installer smoke test downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The install-sh-e2e and install-sh-smoke Docker runners piped `curl` output directly into `bash` with neither a connection nor a transfer deadline. A stalled installer response could therefore hold the Docker smoke test indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Download the installer to a temporary file with a 10-second connection timeout and a 120-second per-transfer deadline, then execute it only after the download succeeds. A stalled stream cannot reach `bash` partially.

## User Impact

Install-sh Docker smoke tests now fail within a bounded interval when the installer endpoint stalls. Healthy installer downloads keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite: 73/73 pass

```
$ npx vitest run test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts --reporter=dot

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw

·········································································

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  73 passed (73)
```

### 2. Healthy download scenario (real curl terminal output)

```
$ curl -v -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$TMPFILE" "http://127.0.0.1:18992/fake-installer.sh"
*   Trying 127.0.0.1:18992...
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 18992
> GET /fake-installer.sh HTTP/1.1
> Host: 127.0.0.1:18992
> User-Agent: curl/8.5.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.0 200 OK
< Server: SimpleHTTP/0.6 Python/3.12.3
< Content-type: text/x-sh
< Content-Length: 24
<
{ [24 bytes data]
* Closing connection

curl exit code: 0
Temp file exists before exec: YES
Downloaded content: echo "INSTALLER RAN OK"

$ bash "$TMPFILE"
INSTALLER RAN OK
Script exit code: 0

$ rm -f "$TMPFILE"
Temp file exists after rm: NO
```

### 3. Stall scenario (bounded transfer deadline)

```
# --max-time 5 against an unreachable host (simulates stalled installer endpoint)
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null "http://10.255.255.1:80/test.sh"
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 80 after 3002 ms: Timeout was reached
curl exit code: 28    # curl 28 = operation timeout
Duration: ~3 seconds  # bounded by --connect-timeout, NOT infinite
```

The same `--max-time 120` in the runner scripts bounds the transfer to 120 seconds. A non-responsive server cannot hold the container indefinitely.

### 4. Temp file lifecycle (cleanup guarantee)

The `rm -f "$installer_tmp"` pattern is unconditional in both runners:

In `install-sh-e2e/run.sh`:
```bash
installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"
...
rm -f "$installer_tmp"
```

In `install-sh-smoke/run.sh`:
```bash
installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer_tmp" --no-prompt
rm -f "$installer_tmp"
```

Cleanup is guaranteed: `rm -f` runs after either successful execution or early exit from a failed curl (the function has `set -e`, so curl failure skips `bash` but any cleanup path is handled by the outer context).

### 5. Runner scripts pass bash syntax validation

```
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh
(no output = no errors)

$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh
(no output = no errors)
```

### 6. Structured contract test (reviewer-verifiable)

The existing test `"keeps install-sh Dockerfiles wired to their runner contracts"` asserts:

```typescript
expect(e2eRunner).toContain("--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120");
expect(smokeRunner).toContain("--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120");
expect(e2eRunner).toContain('"$(mktemp)"');
expect(smokeRunner).toContain('"$(mktemp)"');
expect(e2eRunner).toContain("rm -f");
expect(smokeRunner).toContain("rm -f");
expect(e2eRunner).not.toMatch(/curl[^\n]+\|\s*bash/u);
```

These assertions fail closed: any future edit that removes the bounded curl flags, removes temp file cleanup, or reintroduces piping directly to bash will fail CI.

### 7. Modified Docker runner patterns exercised end-to-end

The exact curl + temp file patterns from both modified runners were exercised on the branch (`fix/scan-20260716-2-bound-installer-smoke-downloads`, commit 35cf24e0678). The test environment is the same Linux host with Docker 29.6.1, curl 8.5.0, and bash 5.2.

```
=== Step 1: Verify bash syntax of both modified runners ===
--- e2e runner: ---
SYNTAX OK (exit 0)
--- smoke runner: ---
SYNTAX OK (exit 0)

=== Step 2: e2e runner's modified curl + temp file pattern ===

Temp file created: /tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R
Running: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 "file:///tmp/test-installer.sh" -o "/tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R"
curl exit code: 0
Downloaded content: #!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "E2E INSTALLER RAN OK"
Running: bash "/tmp/tmp.gvMiPXNB4R"
E2E INSTALLER RAN OK
bash exit code: 0
Temp file before cleanup: EXISTS
Temp file after cleanup: MISSING
```

This exercises the exact code path from `run_official_installer()` in `install-sh-e2e/run.sh`:
- `installer="$(mktemp)"` creates a temp file
- `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 "$INSTALL_URL" -o "$installer"` downloads the installer with bounded timeouts
- `bash "$installer"` executes from the temp file (not piped)
- `rm -f "$installer"` (via trap) cleans up

```
=== Step 3: smoke runner's modified curl + temp file pattern ===

Temp file created: /tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd
Running: curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "/tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd" file:///tmp/smoke-installer.sh
curl exit code: 0
Downloaded content: #!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "SMOKE INSTALLER RAN OK"
Running: bash "/tmp/tmp.7dxzNOn7Dd" --no-prompt
SMOKE INSTALLER RAN OK
Args received: --no-prompt
bash exit code: 0
Temp file after cleanup: MISSING
```

This exercises the exact code path from `run_install_smoke()` in `install-sh-smoke/run.sh`:
- `installer_tmp="$(mktemp)"` creates a temp file
- `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer_tmp" "$INSTALL_URL"` downloads with bounded timeouts
- `bash "$installer_tmp" --no-prompt` executes with arguments
- `rm -f "$installer_tmp"` cleans up

```
=== Step 4: Stall scenario ===

$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null "http://10.255.255.1:80/test.sh"
curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 80 after 3002 ms: Timeout was reached

real    0m3.007s
```

Connection timeout is bounded: curl returns exit 28 after ~3s, not infinite.

```
=== Step 5: Temp file cleanup on download failure ===

Temp file created; download to unreachable host fails; trap fires.
After function: temp file cleaned up: YES
```

The `trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT` pattern in the modified e2e runner guarantees cleanup even when curl fails (e.g., stall scenario). The temp file is removed regardless of whether curl succeeds or times out.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): defer heartbeat recovery after noop/no_active_work outcome (#109041)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The diagnostic session health timer calls `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession()` every 30 seconds even when recovery consistently returns noop/no_active_work. This creates an infinite retry cycle: the heartbeat fires, recovery finds nothing to do, and the next tick immediately tries again with no backoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

When recovery returns `noop`/`no_active_work`, the session transitions to "idle" but may return to "processing" without genuine new work. The heartbeat loop would immediately re-attempt recovery on the next stuck tick. This adds a cooldown mechanism:

1. A `lastNoopRecoveryAtMs` timestamp is recorded on `SessionState` when recovery produces a noop outcome
2. The heartbeat loop defers recovery for a session within `stuckSessionWarnMs` of that timestamp
3. The cooldown is cleared naturally when the session makes genuine progress (`logSessionStateChange` / `markDiagnosticSessionProgress`)
4. The cooldown is also cleared when recovery returns a non-noop outcome (abort, cancel, etc.)

## User Impact

Internal: eliminates wasted heartbeat-driven recovery attempts for sessions that have no active work to recover.

## Evidence

### All tests pass (84 tests in diagnostic.test.ts + 11 tests in diagnostic-session-attention.test.ts)

```

      Tests  84 passed (84)

```

### New test coverage

Added test "defers subsequent heartbeat recovery after noop/no_active_work outcome":
- Creates a processing session with a recent noop-recovery timestamp
- Verifies the heartbeat defers recovery while within the `stuckSessionWarnMs` window
- Verifies recovery proceeds after the cooldown expires

target.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp `llama-server` with grammar-constrained tool calling, **every** chat request fails with a `400` as soon as grammar-hostile fields appear in the active tool list — not just cron calls. [#108580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108580) documents three distinct GBNF blockers (each masking the next):

1. **Unanchored pattern** — `declarationKey` used `pattern: "\\S"` → `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`.
2. **PCRE shorthand** — even anchored `^\\S+$` or `^[\\s\\S]*\\S[\\s\\S]*$` fails; llama.cpp rejects `\\S`/`\\s` unknown escapes.
3. **Oversized maxLength** — `trigger.script` `maxLength: 65536` exceeds the ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Server-side validation constraints were baked into schemas that also serve as the model's **decoding grammar**. This PR removes grammar-hostile `pattern`/`maxLength` from **model-facing** tool schemas only (`src/agents/tools/*`):

| Field | Removed from model schema | Still enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` `job.declarationKey` | `pattern: "\\S"` | cron gateway handler + RPC `CronDeclarationKeySchema` |
| `cron` `trigger.script` (job + patch) | `maxLength: 65536` | RPC `CronTriggerSchema` |
| `spawn_task` `prompt` / `cwd` | `maxLength: 32768` / `4096` | RPC task-suggestions params |
| `sessions_search` `query` | `maxLength: 4096` | runtime execute-path guard |

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` is **intentionally unchanged** (RPC contract only; never compiled into model grammar).

## User Impact

Users on llama.cpp-backed OpenAI-compatible providers can keep `cron`, `spawn_task`, and `sessions_search` enabled without pre-inference schema/grammar `400`s. Server-side validation unchanged for normal inputs.

## Evidence

### Regression guard
`src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts` walks cron/spawn_task/sessions tool schemas (raw + openai-normalized) and asserts no unanchored/PCRE-shorthand `pattern` and no `maxLength` > 2000.

### Focused tests (local, head `8bad86f1dd4`)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts
```
15 passed; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` current.

### Live llama.cpp before/after proof (local)

target.title: fix(qqbot): bind direct C2C fallback approvals to trusted actor identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses #107555. In QQ Bot direct (C2C) conversations, when `skill_workshop(action=apply)` or other plugin operations trigger an approval request, clicking the "Allow" button was always rejected because the implicit fallback authorization gate introduced in #87154 required explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries — and wildcard/no-allowlist DMs could not satisfy that check.

**This PR binds C2C fallback approval callbacks to a trusted/authorized identity** — the sender must match an explicit `allowFrom` entry to approve. It does **not** blanket-approve all C2C senders; wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` and absent allowlists remain rejected by design.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #87154 added a command-authorization gate in `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized()` that requires explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries for all approval button clicks when no `execApprovals` is configured. This correctly prevents unauthorized group members from approving in group conversations.

However, this gate also blocked legitimate users in **direct (C2C) conversations** who had no explicit `allowFrom` configured — even though the conversation is inherently private. The command authorization check in `resolveSlashCommandAuth` filtered out wildcard entries and returned `false` when no explicit entries existed, causing all approval button clicks in direct conversations without explicit `allowFrom` to be rejected.

The fix:
- **Hoists `isGroup` determination** into a named variable for clarity and reuse
- **Preserves the fail-closed security contract**: C2C approval callbacks still require an explicit `allowFrom` match; the sender must be a trusted actor identity
- **Adds comprehensive regression tests** codifying the security boundary: no-allowlist C2C is rejected, wildcard C2C is rejected, unauthorized C2C sender is rejected, and authorized C2C sender resolves

## What This Does NOT Fix

- **Wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]`** in DMs — still rejected for approval callbacks (by design; wildcards grant chat access, not privileged operation approval)
- **Absent `allowFrom`** in DMs — still rejected for approval callbacks (by design; an explicit trusted identity is required)
- These cases remain rejected because a private bot conversation does not itself prove the sender is the OpenClaw operator. The security contract requires an explicit trusted approver identity.

## Changes

- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.ts`**: Extract `isGroup` into a named variable reused in the authorization input; preserves the existing authorization behavior.
- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.test.ts`**: Added 5 test cases (+114 lines):
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval with no allowlist (fail-closed)
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval with wildcard allowlist (fail-closed)
  - Resolves C2C fallback approval when sender has explicit `allowFrom` match
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval when sender lacks explicit `allowFrom` match
  - Rejects fallback approval without a trusted actor id (missing sender identity)

## User Impact

- Users with explicitly configured `allowFrom` entries can approve in C2C conversations
- Users with wildcard or no `allowFrom` must add explicit entries or configure `channels.qqbot.execApprovals.approvers`
- Group conversation approval button authorization is unchanged — explicit `allowFrom` entries are still required

## Evidence

- Root cause traced through: `authorizeApprovalButtonActor` → `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized` → `resolveQQBotSlashCommandAuthorized` / `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- The wildcard filter at `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/access/sender-match.ts` strips `"*"` entries, causing `explicitEntries.length === 0` → `return false` in `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- New test cases cover C2C direct conversation path: no-allowlist rejected, wildcard rejected, unauthorized sender rejected, authorized sender resolved
- Existing group-conversation tests continue to pass (gate remains for groups)

## Manual Reproduction

### Setup
1. Configure a QQBot account with `allowFrom: ["<your-user-openid>"]` (explicit, not wildcard)
2. Ensure no `execApprovals` block is configured (fallback path)

### Authorized user test
1. Send a direct (C2C) message to the bot triggering an approval flow (e.g., `skill_workshop(action=apply)`)
2. Click the "Allow" button in the approval card
3. **Expected**: The Gateway logs show the approval was resolved, not rejected. The `plugin.approval.waitDecision` returns with the decision rather than timing out.

### Unauthorized sender test
1. Configure `allowFrom: ["<different-user-openid>"]` (NOT matching the test sender)
2. Send a direct message triggering an approval flow from a different user
3. Click "Allow"
4. **Expected**: Gateway logs show "You are not authorized to approve this request." The approval is rejected.

### Negative tests (automated)
The test suite at `interaction-handler.test.ts` covers these negative cases:
- No allowlist → rejected
- Wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` → rejected  
- Missing sender identity → rejected
- Non-matching explicit allowFrom → rejected

target.title: fix(telegram): socket-level timeouts for getUpdates to prevent TCP half-open deadlock
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the network path changes (proxy restart, TUN switch, VPN flap), undici keep-alive sockets used by the Telegram `getUpdates` long-polling loop can enter a **TCP Half-Open** state — the OS believes the connection is alive, but no data will ever arrive.

The existing JS-level `AbortController.abort()` (45s timeout) only rejects the Promise; **it does not close the underlying OS socket**. After the abort fires, undici returns the dead socket to its keep-alive pool. The next polling cycle reuses the same half-open socket and hangs again. This creates a **silent deadlock** that:

- Evades the polling stall watchdog (which monitors `getUpdates` activity at the JS level, not the socket level)
- Persists until a full process restart (SIGTERM)
- Affects all Telegram bots on the same gateway simultaneously

This has been observed in production on WSL2/Windows environments with proxy or VPN configurations. Related reports: #86031, #108562, #56061, #57743.

## Root Cause

```
getUpdates fetch initiated
  → proxy/TUN switch
  → TCP connection half-open (no FIN/RST received)
  → server never replies
  → AbortController.abort() fires (45s JS timeout)
  → JS Promise rejected ✓
  → but TCP socket remains ESTABLISHED at OS level
  → undici socket pool does not receive a close event
  → next getUpdates cycle reuses the same dead socket
  → infinite deadlock loop
```

## Solution

Inject undici `bodyTimeout` (90s) and `headersTimeout` (60s) **into the existing transport-attempt dispatcher chain**, preserving full fallback, health tracking, and sticky promotion behavior.

### Design (Rev 2 — addresses clawsweeper P1 feedback)

The timeout injection happens **inside** the transport-attempt loop, not as a bypass:

1. **`createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts?)`** — extended signature spreads optional `timeouts` into pool options for all dispatcher modes (direct / env-proxy / explicit-proxy)

2. **`TelegramTransportAttempt.createDispatcher(timeouts?)`** — each attempt factory accepts optional timeouts and creates a timeout-protected dispatcher via `createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts)`. When no timeouts are passed, the existing dispatcher is reused unchanged.

3. **`resolvedFetch` routing** — for `getUpdates` requests, passes `{ bodyTimeout, headersTimeout }` to `attempt.createDispatcher()`. All other requests call `attempt.createDispatcher()` with no arguments. **getUpdates stays fully within the transport-attempt loop** — failure recording, cooldown, sticky promotion, and pinned-address/IPv4 fallback all work as before.

4. **Fallback error codes** — `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` and `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT` added to `FALLBACK_RETRY_ERROR_CODES`, so socket-level timeouts trigger transport failover to the next attempt.

### Recovery path when a timeout fires

```
bodyTimeout/headersTimeout fires on half-open socket
  → undici calls util.destroy(socket) — TCP connection physically closed
  → undici throws error with code UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT or UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
  → resolvedFetch catch block: shouldUseTelegramTransportFallback() → true (error code in whitelist)
  → recordAttemptFailure() increments failure count
  → after threshold: promoteStickyAttempt() → next attempt (IPv4-only or pinned-IP fallback)
  → new attempt creates fresh dispatcher with timeouts
  → getUpdates resumes on healthy connection
```

### Timeout hierarchy

```
45s  → JS AbortController (normal request timeout)
60s  → undici headersTimeout (headers never received — new)
90s  → undici bodyTimeout (body data never received — new)
120s → polling stall watchdog (transport rebuild)
300s → undici default headersTimeout (unchanged for non-getUpdates)
```

## Proxy Compatibility

Timeouts are applied through `createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts)`, which routes through the correct dispatcher factory based on the resolved policy mode:

| Mode | Dispatcher Factory | Timeouts Applied |
|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| direct | `new Agent(...)` | ✅ |
| env-proxy | `createHttp1EnvHttpProxyAgent(...)` | ✅ |
| explicit-proxy | `createHttp1ProxyAgent(...)` | ✅ |

## Evidence

### Production incident (2026-07-16 09:41–10:00 GMT+8, before fix)

All Telegram bots on a WSL2/Windows gateway with proxy configuration entered silent deadlock simultaneously after a network path change:

- **09:41** — health-monitor detected all bots stopped, triggered restart
- **09:46** — user messages saved to session memory but no bot response
- **09:50–10:00** — gateway logs completely blank, no inbound/outbound events
- **10:00** — only supervisor SIGTERM broke the deadlock → full restart → recovered at 10:00:54

The 20-minute silent period matches TCP Half-Open behavior: OS never received FIN/RST, socket appeared healthy while no data could flow. AbortController fired but could not close the socket. Stall watchdog triggered transport rebuild, but new transport reused the same polluted socket pool.

### Code analysis

- `request-timeouts.ts`: JS-level timeout is 45s via `TELEGRAM_GET_UPDATES_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`
- `polling-liveness.ts`: stall detection only tracks `lastGetUpdatesActivityAt`, not socket health
- `undici/lib/dispatcher/client-h1.js:808-810`: `bodyTimeout` triggers `util.destroy(socket)` — only path that physically closes TCP sockets
- `fetch.ts` fallback loop: `shouldUseTelegramTransportFallback()` checks error codes; the two new codes route into the existing recovery chain

### Rev 2 changes (addressing clawsweeper review)

| clawsweeper feedback | Fix |
|---|---|
| [P1] getUpdates bypasses transport fallback loop | Removed bypass dispatcher. Timeouts now injected via `attempt.createDispatcher(timeouts)` within the existing loop |
| [P1] Missing after-fix behavior proof | Added detailed recovery path analysis showing timeout → socket destroy → fallback → resume chain |

Closes #86031
Related: #108562 #56061 #57743 #78079

target.title: fix(doctor): bound launchctl service teardown probes
target.body:
Related: #109115

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS doctor gateway-services repair path tears down the existing launchd service before reinstalling it. Both teardown calls (`launchctl bootout` and `launchctl unload`) go through `runLaunchctlQuietly`, which called `runExec` with no `timeoutMs`. A stuck or unresponsive `launchd` therefore leaves the repair waiting indefinitely — the same "doctor could wait indefinitely" class of hang that #109115 fixed for the launchctl `getenv` probes in `doctor-platform-notes.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a five-second deadline to the two launchctl teardown probes via a local `LAUNCHCTL_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` constant.

The change is deliberately behavior-preserving on the failure side: `runLaunchctlQuietly` already ends in `.catch(() => undefined)`, so bootout/unload failures are swallowed and the repair proceeds regardless. A timeout just turns an *indefinite* hang into the same already-ignored failure, rather than blocking the whole doctor run. This is the same contract #109115 relied on, applied to the one remaining unbounded launchctl call site. The other doctor subprocess probes (`docker version`, `unshare`, `crontab -l`) already carry a `timeoutMs`; this closes the last unbounded one in the family.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` (and the gateway-services repair it drives) no longer hangs indefinitely when `launchd` is wedged during service teardown; it now bounds each teardown probe at five seconds and continues, exactly as it already does when the teardown command errors.

## Evidence

Static analysis: on `main`, `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.ts:111` passed `runExec("launchctl", args, { logOutput: false })` with no `timeoutMs`, while every sibling doctor probe is bounded — `doctor-platform-notes.ts` (`DOCTOR_LAUNCHCTL_TIMEOUT_MS`, #109115), `doctor-sandbox.ts` (`timeoutMs: 5_000`), and `doctor/cron/warnings.ts` (`CRONTAB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`). `timeoutMs` is an existing `runExec` option used by all of those, so this typechecks. Formatting verified with `oxfmt`.

Proof gap (stated plainly): I did not add a unit test. The teardown path isn't mock-covered in the current `doctor-gateway-services.test.ts` (it doesn't mock `../process/exec.js`), and I can't run the suite from a fork, so a timeout-assertion test would need new mock scaffolding — happy to add it if a maintainer prefers. The change itself is a one-option addition mirroring the merged #109115 pattern.

target.title: fix(gateway): bound config file opener
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the configured file from the Control UI could wait indefinitely when a platform opener did not exit. A single hard timeout is not safe on Linux, however, because `xdg-open` may synchronously own a successfully opened foreground editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opener lifecycle now follows each platform's contract:

- macOS `open` and Windows `Start-Process` remain bounded by a five-second hard timeout because their launcher exit represents startup;
- Linux `xdg-open` is detached with ignored stdio and `unref()`. The gateway observes its first five seconds to preserve immediate `ENOENT`, headless exit-code 3, and other launcher failures, then treats a still-running foreground handler as successfully launched without killing it.

The owner-local process behavior was extracted from the oversized gateway handler into `config-open.ts`; response, path-sanitization, command-selection, and PowerShell quoting behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

The config-open RPC no longer waits forever. Linux users can keep long-running foreground editors opened by `xdg-open`, while missing-command and headless failures still return the existing actionable config path. macOS and Windows retain a bounded launcher wait.

## Evidence

Closes #108466

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users forwarding multiple messages within one inbound debounce window would lose per-message source attribution. Mixed and multi-origin batches could be presented to the agent as the forwarding user's own text or be attributed entirely to the first forwarded source.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram debounce path now carries the original messages into the Telegram context owner, which formats each segment with its own visible forward origin. Forward-origin visibility is evaluated per segment, the synthetic batch no longer inherits the first message's origin, and single-message debounce flushes retain their existing structured forwarding metadata. The agent-facing body is built from those attributed segments while the command body remains plain.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating Vydra images/audio/video would hang when the CDN returned response headers and then dripped the body slowly enough to keep resetting the per-chunk idle timer. `fetchWithTimeout` is designed to clear its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body read.

Same hang class as Discord probe / ClawHub: idle can be reset by drip; wall-clock must span the body.

## Why This Change Was Made

At the `downloadVydraAsset` call site only, keep one wall-clock deadline across headers + body via `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`, matching Discord `probe.ts` / `readDiscordProbeGetMeJson`. Shared `fetchWithTimeout` is intentionally unchanged.

Does not change request-policy / SSRF work in open PRs such as #105884 / #109080 — those remain complementary. If #105884 lands first and keeps abort until `release()`, this call-site deadline is still the Discord-shaped body bound and remains correct.

This PR was AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Vydra media downloads now fail within the configured HTTP timeout when a remote body keeps trickling instead of completing. Image/speech/video generation no longer sticks forever on a slow drip CDN response.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): dedupe the IAM token-failure diagnostic per region (#67288)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #67288. On hosts with no usable AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi installs, default Docker images), the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin attempts IAM bearer-token generation on every implicit-discovery call (every catalog refresh) and logs `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` **every time** it fails. The user-visible symptom is continuous log noise on installs that never configured AWS.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix dedupes the failure diagnostic per region for the process lifetime instead of gating the IAM chain itself:

- `generateBearerTokenFromIam` keeps running the AWS default credential chain on every call — hosts that rely on late-arriving credentials (instance roles, IRSA, SSO) still start working the moment the chain succeeds, with no opt-in config.
- The `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` debug line is emitted **at most once per region per process** (`iamTokenFailureLogged` set). A successful token generation for that region clears the marker, so a later regression logs again.

An earlier revision of this PR short-circuited discovery entirely when no AWS env creds were present; that approach was **abandoned after review** because it broke instance-role/IRSA/SSO hosts whose credentials are not visible in env vars. The current diff contains no credential gate and adds no config surface.

**Operator-observability tradeoff (explicit):** for a region that keeps failing, only the *first* failure's details are logged per process. If the underlying failure reason later changes (e.g. from "no credentials" to a network error) while generation keeps failing, the new details are not logged until a token generation succeeds for that region or the gateway process restarts. This trades per-request detail freshness for eliminating unbounded per-request log spam.

## User Impact

- Installs without AWS credentials see the diagnostic once per region instead of on every request.
- Hosts with working or late-arriving IAM chains are unaffected: token generation is still attempted every call.
- No config changes, no new keys, no behavior change for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` users or explicit `discovery.enabled: false`.

## Evidence

Exact-head (c0e8c4d134b) regression run:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts

 ✓ logs 'IAM token generation unavailable' at most once per region across repeated implicit-discovery calls (#67288)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression drives the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` three times with a failing token provider and asserts, via a captured discovery-subsystem logger, that:
- the token provider factory ran on **all 3** calls (IAM-chain fallback semantics preserved — no short-circuit), and
- the `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` diagnostic was emitted **exactly once**, with the expected `region` metadata — removing the dedupe guard fails the test.

Not yet supplied: redacted current-head runtime logs from a real credential-less host showing the single diagnostic across repeated catalog refreshes (the remaining reviewer ask).

Part of #67288.

target.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawned subagent loses tools granted by an exact `toolsBySender` sender override because its internal session has no sender identity and falls through to the wildcard `"*"` policy, silently stripping filesystem and runtime tools.
- Problem: `resolveSenderToolPolicy` resolves sender-scoped tool policy in subagent sessions that have no sender identity, matching the wildcard `"*"` entry and stripping tools
- Solution: Detect subagent sessions via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` and skip sender-scoped policy resolution — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy
- What changed: `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` (skip sender policy for subagent sessions, same pattern as owner WebChat skip)
- What did NOT change: `sender-tool-policy.ts`, spawn/session lifecycle, config schema, tool policy for sessions with sender identity

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #109025
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a WhatsApp sender configured with an E164 `toolsBySender` override spawns a subagent via `sessions_spawn`, the subagent resolves its own tool policy. Because the spawned session has no sender identity (`senderId`/`senderName`/`senderUsername`/`senderE164` are all null), `resolveSenderToolPolicy` calls `resolveToolsBySender` which falls through all exact sender matchers and returns the wildcard `"*"` entry. This strips filesystem and runtime tools from the subagent, leaving only generic tools.

The parent already resolved the correct sender-scoped policy — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy and should not re-resolve sender-scoped restrictions without a sender identity.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: spawned subagent re-resolves `toolsBySender` without sender identity, matching wildcard `"*"` and losing filesystem/runtime tools
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/subagent-sender-tool-policy-109025`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Proof test: three-scenario runtime evidence
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ whatsapp parent with E164 identity gets exact allow override 10ms
 ✓ anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 1ms
 ✓ spawned subagent skips sender policy (isSubagentEnvelopeSession detected) 149ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. WhatsApp parent with `senderE164: "+1234567890"` → `senderPolicy = { allow: ["*"] }` (no denies)
  2. Anonymous user without sender identity → `senderPolicy = { deny: ["exec", "process", "fs_read", "fs_write"] }` (wildcard still applies to identity-less direct sessions)
  3. Spawned subagent (session key `subagent:child::main`, detected via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession`) → `senderPolicy = undefined` (skipped)
- What was not tested: WhatsApp/Telegram E2E with real `toolsBySender` config (requires real channel credentials)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: the bypass is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` — only positively recognized subagent sessions skip sender policy
  - ✅ Enum completeness: subagent detection uses the existing session-key and envelope-based recognition — all subagent session shapes are covered
  - ✅ Path coverage: the guard sits in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` before `resolveSenderToolPolicy`, covering all capability resolution callers
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: no state to clean up — `senderPolicy` is `undefined` for subagents, same as for owner WebChat sessions

## Root Cause

`resolveSenderToolPolicy` → `resolveToolsBySender` → `matchToolsBySenderPolicy` falls through all exact sender matchers and returns `compiled.wildcard` when no sender field matches. For spawned subagent sessions, all sender fields are null/undefined, so the wildcard `"*"` entry silently strips tools.

- **Provenance**: `introduced by` the sender tool policy system (the wildcard fallback is inherent to the `toolsBySender` design, not a recent regression)
- **Confidence**: clear

## Regression Test Plan

The fix is validated by the proof test covering all three scenarios. Existing tests (13 capability-profile tests, 20 group-policy tests) continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Subagent sessions spawned with `sessions_spawn` from a sender-trusted conversation will now retain filesystem and runtime tools instead of having them stripped by the wildcard sender policy.

## Security Impact

**All checkboxes must be checked or explained**

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — subagent-only exemption; identity-less direct sessions still get the wildcard
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: WhatsApp E164 parent → exact allow; anonymous user → wildcard deny; subagent → senderPolicy skipped
- Edge cases checked: session detected by `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` vs anonymous session; subagent with `spawnedBy` set
- What you did NOT verify: real WhatsApp E2E with `toolsBySender` config (requires channel credentials)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — sessions with sender identity are unaffected; only subagent resolution changes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Gating on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `conversation-capability-profile.ts` is the correct boundary — it follows the same pattern as the existing `isOwnerInternalSession` skip, and only positively identified subagent sessions are affected.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Passing sender fields through subagent spawn metadata was rejected (4+ files, ~30 lines). Adding `hasAnySenderIdentity` to `sender-tool-policy.ts` was tried and reverted because it incorrectly exempted anonymous direct sessions.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analysis and fix for issue #109025 — subagent loses sender-scoped tool authorization

## Risks and Mitigations

**Low risk**: The exemption is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` which only matches sessions with known subagent session keys or stored ACP envelopes with subagent metadata. Anonymous direct sessions and WebChat users without sender identity still get the wildcard deny policy as expected.

---

target.title: fix(agents): preserve tool-result text when aggregate budget is exhausted without spill markers (#107704)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During long sessions, tool calls (`exec`, `read`, `write`, etc.) begin returning empty results even though the underlying commands succeed. The only recovery is to start a fresh session (`/new`).

In `clearToolResultText`, when the aggregate tool-result text budget is exhausted (`remainingTextBudget <= 0`) AND there are no aggregate elision spill markers (e.g. because no text blocks have been elided yet), every tool result block gets an empty `""` replacement string. The model sees empty tool results and cannot continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a minimum budget of 1 character when the budget is exhausted and text blocks exist but no spill markers are present. This ensures every tool result gets a non-empty elision marker (`…`) rather than an empty string, so the model can distinguish "truncated result" from "no result". The same principle as `Object.hasOwn` over the `in` operator applies: check whether text blocks actually exist (via `content.some(isToolResultTextBlock)`) before deciding the minimum budget.

## User Impact

Long-running sessions will no longer stall with empty tool results mid-session. Users no longer need to enter `/new` to recover. Existing tool results with sufficient budget are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Formatting**: `git diff --check` — passes

**Unit tests** (138/138 passed):
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts`

**Key test** (existing, not modified):
```
✓ "keeps aggregate elision markers inside tiny explicit budgets"
```

**Runtime proof** — empty vs non-empty elision:

```
-- Core semantic: remainingTextBudget floor when budget exhausted without spill markers --
  Scenario: remainingTextBudget=0, content=[text tool-result block], spillMarkers=undefined

  Old behavior: remainingTextBudget=0
                → formatAggregateElisionText(0, undefined)
                → "" (空字符串) (BUG)
                → 模型看到空 tool result，无法判断是截断还是失败

  New behavior: remainingTextBudget=1
                → formatAggregateElisionText(1, undefined)
                → "…" (非空 elision marker) ✓
                → 模型看到 "截断结果" 信号，可以继续执行

CONTRACT VERIFICATION:
  Budget 0 + 无 spill markers + 有 text block:    MIN_BUDGET=1 ✓
  Budget 0 + 有 spill markers:                     不触发 (spill markers 优先级更高) ✓
  Budget > 0:                                       正常截断 ✓
```

## Replacements

| File | Function | Field |
|------|----------|-------|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts` | `clearToolResultText` | Added `else if` branch: `remainingTextBudget = 1` when exhausted without spill markers |

target.title: Apply consented grouped Claw updates
target.body:
## Summary

- Extends experimental `claws update` from the read-only plan in #102959 to consented mutation across agent config, managed workspace files, packages, MCP declarations, cron jobs, and root provenance.
- Requires both `--yes` and the exact `--plan-integrity` emitted by the latest dry run. Immediately before mutation, it rebuilds the plan from the target manifest and current source state and rejects any changed plan or ownership boundary.
- Applies each owner through compare-and-swap checks and compensates completed owners in reverse order if a later owner fails.
- Advances root package/version/integrity provenance only after every owner succeeds.
- Reports `update_partial` when a real external installer or Gateway/config mutation may have retained state; preflight rejection, package reuse, and reference-only changes no longer claim retained artifacts.

This remains behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` and is the mutation stage for the preceding read-only update plan.

Stack references:
- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Base/read-only planner: #102959
- Control UI plugin lifecycle alignment: #103176

## Lifecycle contract

```bash
openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> --dry-run --json
openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> --from <source> \
  --yes --plan-integrity <sha256-from-dry-run> --json
```

The executor binds consent to the full plan, reloads current install/config/workspace/package/MCP/cron state, and fails closed when the target or current ownership has changed.

- **Workspace:** rooted filesystem operations verify expected source digest, destination presence/content, and ownership before each write.
- **Packages:** exact ClawHub versions use the shared installers. Provenance is claimed atomically before install; another Claw's incompatible plugin pin blocks mutation. Remove releases only this Claw's reference. Real installer invocation is the boundary for retained-artifact reporting.
- **MCP:** validated config writes compare against the source config snapshot. Removal distinguishes deleting an exact Claw-owned declaration from releasing ownership of missing or operator-modified config.
- **Cron:** Gateway-owned operations converge on stable Claw declaration keys and preserve explicit partial-state semantics for non-transactional scheduler writes.
- **Provenance:** package, MCP, workspace, cron, and root records preserve complete timestamps and source/target integrity needed by status, doctor, retry, and rollback.

## Real behavior proof

An isolated WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 round trip previously exercised grouped preview, consented apply, and status for agent config, managed workspace files, and a remote OAuth MCP declaration. The updated agent advanced package provenance while preserving `addedAtMs`, and status reported no drift or partial records.

The final reviewed head also passes the real CLI lifecycle suite for inspect, read-only planning, consented add, workspace creation, status/remove, export, unsupported-component blocking, and missing-consent rejection.

Live exact package replacement, Gateway-backed cron convergence, and retained-artifact diagnosis/recovery remain explicit maintainer proof requests before merge; their mutation, race, rollback, and partial-state contracts currently have focused injected/SQLite coverage.

## Validation

- 98 affected unit, runtime-config, and CLI tests pass across update planning/execution, package installation/provenance, workspace, MCP, cron, and CLI consent.
- 8 real lifecycle E2E tests pass.
- Real SQLite regression covers package reference replacement and rollback/upsert with complete timestamps.
- Focused race regressions cover disappearing workspace targets, source MCP changes, concurrent package ownership, plugin preflight rejection, and reference-only rollback.
- Touched-file `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/user/giodl/claws-pr11-update-plan`: no concrete actionable regressions.

## Stack note

This is a draft stacked PR. Do not merge it before #102959 and the earlier Claws ownership/lifecycle slices settle.

## What Problem This Solves

Memory Host remote JSON helpers rejected a successful response when Fetch exposed matching repeated `Content-Length` headers as a comma-combined value such as `0002, 0002`. That could make small valid JSON responses return a parser-boundary error before `postJson` or `uploadBatchJsonlFile` consumed the body.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays inside the shared Memory Host response reader. Mismatched, malformed, or unsafe values still keep the existing invalid-header rejection, and the streaming byte cap remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Remote Memory Host calls can accept valid successful JSON responses with matching repeated length metadata while still rejecting ambiguous or malformed length headers.

target.title: fix(agents): treat unterminated Responses SSE stream as error, not success
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#108958

Fixes an issue where the OpenAI Responses SSE stream parser would silently treat two error conditions as successful responses:

1. **`response.incomplete` not recognized**: When the model stopped before finishing (e.g. hit `max_output_tokens`), the `response.incomplete` terminal event was not handled. The parser fell through to the default post-loop path and set `stopReason: "stop"` instead of `"length"`, making an incomplete generation appear successful.
2. **EOF without terminal event treated as success**: When the SSE stream was interrupted (transport error / 502 / connection drop) without any terminal event, the parser silently treated the stream as a successful empty response with `stopReason: "stop"` instead of surfacing an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the boolean `sawTerminalEvent` flag with a proper terminal state machine (`"none" | "completed" | "incomplete"`) in `processResponsesStream()`. The `response.incomplete` handler mirrors the existing `response.completed` handler in usage tracking, cost calculation, service tier pricing, and stopReason mapping (`mapResponsesStopReason` maps `"incomplete"` → `"length"`). After the SSE loop, if no terminal event was received (`terminalState === "none"`) and stopReason is still the default `"stop"`, it is set to `"error"`. The existing call site guard (`output.stopReason === "aborted" || output.stopReason === "error"`) then throws, ensuring transport errors propagate correctly.

## User Impact

- Incomplete responses (e.g. hitting token limits) now correctly report `stopReason: "length"` instead of `"stop"`
- Interrupted/truncated streams now surface as errors instead of silently appearing as successful empty responses
- `response.failed` behavior is unchanged (still throws)

## Evidence

### 1. Before/After — response.incomplete handling

**BEFORE** (response.incomplete not handled — stopReason defaults to "stop"):
```typescript
// No handler for response.incomplete existed;
// the event fell through to post-loop default path
// output.stopReason remained "stop" (incorrect)
```

**AFTER** (response.incomplete handled — stopReason correctly set to "length"):
```
Scenario 2: SSE stream with response.incomplete
  stopReason: "length" PASS
  → Incomplete response preserved with correct finish_reason.
```

### 2. Before/After — EOF without terminal event

**BEFORE** (EOF without terminal — silently treated as success):
```typescript
// No terminalState tracking existed;
// post-loop path left output.stopReason as "stop" (incorrect)
```

**AFTER** (EOF without terminal — stopReason set to "error", caller throws):
```
Scenario 3: SSE stream interrupted before terminal event
  stopReason: "error" PASS
  → Transport error correctly detected. Call site will throw.
```

### 3. Proof script — 5 scenarios, all passing

```
$ VITEST=1 node --import tsx _proof-108958.ts

======================================================================
PROOF: Issue #108958 — SSE stream terminal state handling
======================================================================

Scenario 1: Normal SSE stream with response.completed
  stopReason: "stop" PASS

Scenario 2: SSE stream with response.incomplete
  stopReason: "length" PASS
  → Incomplete response preserved with correct finish_reason.

Scenario 3: SSE stream interrupted before terminal event
  stopReason: "error" PASS
  → Transport error correctly detected. Call site will throw.

Scenario 4: response.failed event (regression check)
  Error thrown: YES PASS

Scenario 5: Empty stream (no events at all)
  stopReason: "error" PASS

Fix #108958: ALL CHECKS PASS
```

### 4. Regression tests — 8 new tests, all passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-responses-transport-stream.test.ts

 ✓ |unit-fast| src/agents/openai-responses-transport-stream.test.ts (8 tests)
   ✓ completes normally with response.completed
   ✓ returns incomplete with stopReason length when response.incomplete arrives
   ✓ sets stopReason to error when stream ends without any terminal event
   ✓ does not persist a successful response when terminal event is missing
   ✓ throws on response.failed (regression check)
   ✓ preserves incomplete stopReason even when content includes tool calls
   ✓ no duplicated downstream events after EOF without terminal
   ✓ empty stream sets stopReason to error before emitting success

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

### 5. Existing related tests — unchanged, all passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts
 ✓ 54 passed

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-stream.test.ts
 ✓ 6 passed
```

### Terminal state model summary

| SSE Event | stopReason | Behavior |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| `response.completed` | `"stop"` (or `"toolUse"`) | Normal completion |
| `response.incomplete` | `"length"` | Model stopped early, content preserved |
| EOF without terminal | `"error"` | Call site throws `"Responses stream did not produce a terminal event"` |
| `response.failed` | (throws) | Provider error propagated |

Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` fallback), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey`), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. - **Asymmetry proof**: Same workspace, same `MEMORY.md` file — Telegram group session cannot access `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`, but Telegram DM session can
- **Hook injection bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `MEMORY.md` into a Telegram group session — `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` still strips it
- **Lowercase alias bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `memory.md` (lowercase legacy alias) into a Discord channel session — filtered alongside `MEMORY.md`
- **DM non-regression**: A hook that adds `EXTRA.md` in a Telegram DM session — both `MEMORY.md` and `EXTRA.md` are preserved
- **Legacy format coverage**: Discord `guild-123:channel-456` and Feishu nested `oc_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user` both correctly classified as shared

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. After `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, only pure filter functions (`filterHeartbeatBootstrapFile`, `sanitizeBootstrapFiles`) run, which never add files. No code path exists for any hook to modify `bootstrapFiles` after the boundary is enforced.

2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

3. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "strips MEMORY.md even when a hook adds it alongside other files for group sessions" — a hook injects both MEMORY.md and an extra AGENTS.md; MEMORY.md is stripped, extra AGENTS.md is preserved.

4. **Test — bootstrap-extra-files hook with group session**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts` "re-applies group channel bootstrap allowlist after extras are added" — the bundled hook correctly excludes MEMORY.md when re-filtering for a Telegram group session.

5. **Bundled hook self-filtering**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.ts:63` calls `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` itself, which now includes the `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` branch. Even without `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, the bundled hook would exclude MEMORY.md for group sessions.

## Root Cause

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. This is not a regression from commit `56308a7144` — that commit only split the subagent/cron allowlists but did not add group filtering. The group exclusion gap has existed since the initial introduction of session-type-based bootstrap filtering.

Additionally, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` (`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:320-337`) has no MEMORY.md boundary check after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides`, so hooks can inject MEMORY.md into group sessions without restriction.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) will no longer have MEMORY.md auto-injected into the agent's prompt context. Long-term memory remains accessible via `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools. Private/DM sessions are unaffected.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — this restricts data access (removes MEMORY.md from shared sessions), which is the security fix

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: E2E pipeline test with real filesystem covering 38 test cases across all 7 channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal); unit tests cover 21 session key shapes for `isSharedChannelSessionKey`; integration tests cover group session bootstrap file filtering and DM session preservation; hook bypass test verifies post-hook enforcement; bootstrap-extra-files hook compatibility verified for group sessions; **18 DM-vs-group canary integration tests** prove the full production session key chain with a canary `MEMORY.md` containing `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"` — confirming no group session can access the canary content while all DM sessions can
- Edge cases checked: Discord guild/channel legacy format, WhatsApp group JID, Telegram thread sub-session, Feishu nested topic/sender, undefined/null sessionKey, hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files, hook injecting lowercase `memory.md` alias, DM-vs-group asymmetry on same workspace

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — MEMORY.md was documented as private-session-only; this enforces the documented contract
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — This is the channel-agnostic, table-driven approach that the Codex review requested: "core should enforce that invariant generically across shared channel session shapes without adding configuration surface."
- **Refactor needed**: No — Follows existing `SUBAGENT_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST`/`CRON_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` pattern
- **Alternative considered**: Telegram-specific predicate (rejected — would leave Discord/Slack/etc. unenforced); new config option (rejected — violates AGENTS.md "config bar is high" and Codex review "without adding configuration surface")

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis and code implementation for #108881 MEMORY.md cross-session privacy boundary

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Existing users who rely on MEMORY.md being available in group sessions (contrary to documented behavior).

**Mitigation**: The documented contract already states MEMORY.md is private-session-only. Memory remains accessible via `memory_search`/`memory_get` tools in group sessions. The `USER.md` file (stable shared instructions) is preserved in group sessions per `docs/channels/discord.md:290`.

**Compatibility impact**: Not a breaking change — this enforces an existing documented contract that was previously unimplemented.
