target.title: fix(line): deliver rich replies on the reply token instead of the push quota
target.body: Closes #65656 Closes #109006 ## What Problem This Solves Ask a LINE bot on a free plan for something that comes back as a table, and once the account's monthly push quota is spent the explanation arrives but **the table silently does not**. Nothing tells the user anything is missing — they just get half an answer. The reporter's log line is `line final reply failed: HTTPFetchError: 429 -`, and their workaround was to ask the agent for raw Markdown so the table never became a Flex bubble at all. On paid plans the table still arrives, but as a detached second bubble that burns a quota message. The same batch also loses its quick reply buttons whenever a reply carries more than five rich bubbles: the buttons are attached to the fifth message, the sixth is pushed straight after, and LINE hides quick replies as soon as a newer message arrives. The offered actions are simply not there. ## Why This Change Was Made A LINE reply token carries up to five messages and costs nothing; push spends the account's monthly allowance. That is the entire reason this delivery path uses the batch APIs at all. But the path only put *text* on the token — the rich and media bubbles were handed to push afterwards: ```ts // before, extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts await deps.sendLineReplyChunks({ ... }); // text -> reply token await sendLineMessages(richMessages, false); // table/flex -> push -> 429 await sendLineMessages(mediaMessages, false); ``` So on a spent quota the table was pushed into a 429 and dropped, while four reply-token slots sat unused. Worth flagging for anyone reading the diff: the hard-coded `false` in those calls looks like the lever, but it isn't. `reply-chunks.ts` sets `replyTokenUsed = true` in its `catch` as well as on success, so by the time those lines run the reply branch inside `sendLineMessages` is already unreachable. Flipping `false` to `true` is a no-op — that is what #65673 did before it was closed. The token has to be shared *before* it is consumed, which means assembling one batch. Once text, rich and media are assembled into a single batch, the no-text branch below turns out to be doing the same thing already — same ordering, same `sendLineMessages(..., true)` call — so the two collapse into one path. That is where the second defect surfaced: the surviving branch capped the quick-reply carrier at the last reply-token slot: ```ts const targetIndex = replyToken && !replyTokenUsed ? Math.min(4, combined.length - 1) : combined.length - 1; ``` This is the only quick-reply attach site in the extension that caps the index — `outbound.ts:248` already uses the true last message — and per the LINE documentation buttons disappear when "Your LINE Official Account, the user, or a different member sends a new message in the room", so the trailing push wipes them. Collapsing the branches leaves one attach site with the same rule the push path already uses. Net result is **9 fewer lines than a fix for the table alone** would have needed (273 → 282 effective source lines, two defects), because the duplicated assembly is gone rather than doubled. ## User Impact - Replies that mix text with a table, Flex card, template, location or media now arrive **complete** on free-plan accounts with a spent push quota, instead of losing the bubble to a 429. - Those replies stop consuming push quota entirely when they fit in five messages, so the monthly allowance lasts longer for the proactive sends that actually need it. - Quick reply buttons now appear on replies carrying more than five bubbles. - No visible change otherwise: ordering is unchanged (text leads, or the bubbles lead when quick replies are present), and anything past the five-message limit still pushes as before. ## Evidence ### 1. Live LINE Messaging API, before vs after Both runs execute the real `deliverLineAutoReply` against a real LINE channel, driven by a genuine inbound webhook event with a real, signature-verified reply token, replying with the reporter's shape (explanatory text + a Markdown table). `totalUsage` is read from `GET /v2/bot/message/quota/consumption` immediately before and after each run. Identifiers redacted. **BEFORE — `main`** ``` [harness] real LINE event: signature=VALID replyToken=a2344c… POST /v2/bot/message/reply -> HTTP 200 messages: [text("Comparison of real estate investment:\n\nHo Chi Minh City leads on yield.")] POST /v2/bot/message/push -> HTTP 200 messages: [flex(altText="Table")] delivery status: delivered push quota totalUsage: before=11 after=12 DELTA=1 ``` The table goes out over push and spends a quota message. On an exhausted quota that call is the reporter's 429 and the table is gone. **AFTER — this PR** ``` [harness] real LINE event: signature=VALID replyToken=22bf80… POST /v2/bot/message/reply -> HTTP 200 messages: [text("Comparison of real estate investment:\n\nHo Chi Minh City leads on yield."), flex(altText="Table")] (no push call) delivery status: delivered push quota totalUsage: before=12 after=12 DELTA=0 ``` LINE returned two `sentMessages` ids for the single reply call — both bubbles delivered. **`DELTA=1` → `DELTA=0`**: the table no longer depends on push quota, so it can no longer be lost to a 429. | BEFORE — `main` (table pushed) | AFTER — this PR (table on the reply token) | |---|---| | | | Both renders are identical from the user's side, which is the point: the delivery route changed, the experience did not. ### 2. Live LINE Messaging API, quick reply placement Same harness, six numbered Flex bubbles plus `quickReplies: ["Alpha", "Beta"]` and no text, so the batch overflows the five-message reply limit. Observed on LINE for iOS (quick replies do not render on LINE for PC at all). **BEFORE — `main` rule `Math.min(4, …)`** ``` reply -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 1"), flex("Bubble 2"), flex("Bubble 3"), flex("Bubble 4"), flex("Bubble 5") +QUICKREPLY] push -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 6")] status: delivered ``` LINE for iOS: six bubbles arrive, **no Alpha/Beta buttons**. **AFTER — this PR** ``` reply -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 1"), flex("Bubble 2"), flex("Bubble 3"), flex("Bubble 4"), flex("Bubble 5")] push -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 6") +QUICKREPLY] status: delivered ``` LINE for iOS: six bubbles arrive, **Alpha/Beta buttons render above the input bar**. | BEFORE — `main` (no buttons) | AFTER — this PR (buttons render) | |---|---| | | | ### 3. Red/green Reverting only `auto-reply-delivery.ts` to `origin/main` (e5240b997e9) and keeping the tests: ``` × sends text and rich messages on one reply token instead of pushing the rich bubble × keeps an extracted markdown table on the reply token alongside text × keeps media on the reply token alongside text × pushes the whole bundled batch when the reply token call fails × keeps quick replies on the trailing bubble when the batch overflows the reply token × sends rich messages before quick-reply text so quick replies remain visible ✓ pushes only the messages that do not fit the reply token batch ✓ tags a later chunk failure after the reply batch without replaying delivered text ✓ uses reply token for rich-only payloads ✓ surfaces a visible partial delivery when an overflow bubble fails alongside quick-reply text ✓ surfaces a visible partial delivery when an overflow bubble fails after text without quick replies ✓ wraps a non-extensible rich failure without losing visible-send evidence ✓ falls back to push when reply token delivery fails ✓ honors channelData.line.mediaKind on the reply-token path instead of forcing image … (18 passed) Tests 6 failed | 18 passed (24) ``` With the fix applied: ``` Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 24 passed (24) ``` The five-or-fewer-bubbles case is covered on both sides of the quick-reply change (`uses reply token for rich-only payloads` stays green throughout — that rule is unchanged below the limit). ### 4. Full checks ``` $ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line/src Test Files 28 passed (28) Tests 361 passed | 1 skipped (362) $ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit -> exit 0 $ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/line -> exit 0 $ oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.test.ts All matched files use the correct format. $ node scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mjs -> exit 0 ``` (`bot-message-context.test.ts` is excluded from the suite line above: it fails on this machine before any change, because Node 22.16 ships SQLite 3.49.1 and OpenClaw requires 3.51.3+. Unrelated to this diff.) ### 5. What was not tested - **The 429 itself.** The account's push quota was not exhausted, so no live `429` was observed. The quota-consumption delta is the proxy: `DELTA=1` means the table depends on the push allowance and therefore inherits its 429; `DELTA=0` means it no longer touches that allowance at all. The reporter's log supplies the 429 half. - **LINE for Android.** Quick replies were verified on LINE for iOS only. LINE for PC renders no quick replies at all, so it cannot exercise that path. - **Overflow beyond ten messages.** The push batching loop (`for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i += 5)`) is unchanged by this PR and already covered. ### 6. References - LINE — reply API carries up to five messages, quota-free: https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#send-reply-message - LINE — rate limits and push quota: https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#rate-limits - LINE — quick reply support and disappearance rules: https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/using-quick-reply/

target.title: fix(trajectory): clean runtime files after short reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory cleanup could leave an external runtime JSONL file behind when the filesystem returned a permitted short positional read. The pointer was removed, but the truncated ownership header could not prove that the matching runtime file belonged to the deleted session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bounded 64 KiB ownership-header read now uses the existing fill-until-EOF helper before applying the same schema, source, session-id, basename, and path checks. The main risk is deleting an unrelated external file; those ownership checks are unchanged, and the regression still verifies that an unsafe non-matching target remains untouched.

## User Impact

Deleted sessions no longer leave proven trajectory runtime files behind on network-backed or otherwise short-reading filesystems, while unrelated external files remain protected by the existing cleanup guards.

## Evidence

Node documents that `fs.read()` may return fewer bytes than requested, including on slow network filesystems, and `fs.readSync()` follows that contract: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fsreadsyncfd-buffer-offset-length-position

Real filesystem behavior proof on Linux/Node 24 used an `LD_PRELOAD` shim that capped `pread` to 16 bytes only for the external runtime JSONL file, while calling the production `removeSessionTrajectoryArtifacts` function.

Latest `upstream/main` (`b3301e32127de6b5ca9ca6b7c0defe0f9c80434a`):

```text
{"removed":["pointer"],"runtimeExists":true}
```

Patched head (`60df0b8db55b7b1fc00b37d92f76b8bbc8fc84b2`), same harness and target:

```text
{"removed":["pointer","runtime"],"runtimeExists":false}
```

Focused regression:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/trajectory/cleanup.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed (4)
```

Reverting only the production read made the short-read case fail before the external runtime could be removed; restoring the helper passed all four tests. `CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main --head HEAD -- src/trajectory/cleanup.ts src/trajectory/cleanup.test.ts` passed formatting, core and core-test typechecks, targeted lint, Plugin SDK baseline, boundary, database-first, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing guards.

`.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output` reported no accepted or actionable findings (`patch is correct`, 0.93 confidence).

AI-assisted: Codex identified the adoption gap, implemented the bounded read, and ran the focused, changed-gate, negative-control, and real-process proof manually.

target.title: fix(ui): add timeout to control-ui bootstrap config fetch
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `loadApplicationConfig` in the Control-UI bootstrap does not set a deadline on its config endpoint fetch. If the server stops responding, the retry loop over auth candidates hangs indefinitely for each attempt, blocking the entire UI startup.

**Solution**: Add `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` to the config endpoint `fetch()` call. When the server does not respond within 15 seconds, the signal aborts, the fetch rejects with a `TimeoutError`, the caller's `try/catch` returns `null`, and the UI proceeds without the server-provided config (gracefully falling back to defaults).

**What changed / NOT changed**: One new constant `CONFIG_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) and one `signal` parameter added to the existing `fetch()` call in `ui/src/app/config.ts`. No API, CLI, config surface, or public interface changed. No dependencies added.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — timeout addition to a background bootstrap fetch. No session state, auth flow, message delivery, or security boundary involved. Failure path (timeout → catch → return null) already exists for other errors.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Stalled config endpoint fetch now aborts after 15 seconds instead of hanging indefinitely, allowing the UI to proceed with default config. The fix follows the same AbortSignal.timeout pattern used in earlier browser screenshot fetch timeout fixes.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (local workstation, three tiers: vitest unit tests, real-time network evidence with the exact production 15s timeout, and real browser-path evidence via Playwright/Chromium).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. `npx vitest run ui/src/app/config.test.ts` — unit test covering timeout behavior (passed 2/2). The test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` to control the AbortSignal.timeout timer and a mock fetch that never resolves, verifying the deadline abort fires at exactly 15 seconds.
2. `node docs/.local/scan-20260715-01/config-fetch-timeout-proof.mjs` — **production-value 15s real-time evidence**: exercises the exact fetch signature (GET, `Accept: application/json`, `credentials: "same-origin"`, `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)`) against a genuinely stalled local HTTP endpoint at the exact URL path `/control-ui-config.json`. Two cases tested:
   - **Stalled endpoint**: request aborted at ~15003ms wall-clock time, demonstrating graceful fallback to default config.
   - **Slow successful response at 14s**: a deliberately slow server that responds at 14s (just under the 15s deadline) successfully delivered config metadata — confirming that latency within the deadline preserves server-provided routing, version, identity, and authentication metadata.
3. `node docs/.local/scan-20260715-01/browser-path-evidence.mjs` — **real browser-path (Playwright/Chromium) evidence**: a headless Chromium browser loaded a minimal HTML page that exercises the exact fetch pattern from `loadApplicationConfig` (AbortSignal.timeout(15_000), GET `/control-ui-config.json`, `Accept: application/json`, `credentials: "same-origin"`) against a stalled endpoint. The browser's fetch call aborted with `TimeoutError` after ~15004ms, confirming the patched behavior works in a real browser context.

**After-fix evidence**:
- Unit test output: `Tests 2 passed (2)` with COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0 (see `docs/.local/scan-20260715-01/verify.log`).
- **Production-value 15s real-time evidence** (`config-fetch-timeout-proof.mjs`):
  ```
  ==============================================================
    Config Fetch Timeout: Real-Time Evidence
    Date: 2026-07-16T14:40:00.339Z
    Node: v25.9.0
  ==============================================================
  --- Test 1: Stalled /control-ui-config.json at 15s timeout ---
  [server]  <- stalled GET /control-ui-config.json -- will not respond
  [client]  elapsed: 15003ms
  [client]  error name: TimeoutError
  [client]  -> GRACEFUL FALLBACK (returns null, UI uses defaults)
    PROOF: Stalled endpoint aborted at ~15000ms.
    Without fix: fetch would hang indefinitely, blocking UI startup.

  --- Test 2: Slow successful response at 14s (under 15s cutoff) ---
  [server]  <- slow /control-ui-config.json -- responding after 14000ms
  [server]  -> responded after 14000ms
  [client]  elapsed: 14009ms
  [client]  response: {"assistantName":"Assistant","serverVersion":"1.2.3","terminalEnabled":true}
  [client]  -> CONFIG LOADED SUCCESSFULLY (within 15s window)
    PROOF: Response at ~14s was received before the 15s deadline.
    Server metadata (version, terminal, identity) preserved.
  ```
- **Real browser-path (Playwright/Chromium) evidence**:
  ```
  [stall-server] listening on :41347, stalled at http://127.0.0.1:41347/control-ui-config.json
  [html-server]  serving test page at http://127.0.0.1:45925/
  --- Browser path: launching Chromium ---
  [stall-server] <- stalled GET /control-ui-config.json -- hanging
  [browser]  waiting for timeout result...
  [browser]  status: TIMEOUT
  [browser]  error: TimeoutError
  [browser]  elapsed: 15004ms
  [browser]  result: Graceful fallback (returned null, UI uses defaults)
  [browser]  screenshot saved to /tmp/evidence-108083/browser-path-evidence.png

  BROWSER PATH PROOF: PASS
  - Real browser (Chromium) exercised the exact fetch pattern.
  - Stalled endpoint timed out at ~15004ms.
  - Error name: TimeoutError (expected).
  - Graceful fallback confirmed (returns null, UI uses defaults).
  - Screenshot: docs/.local/scan-20260715-01/browser-path-evidence.png
  ```

**Observed result after the fix**:
- Stalled endpoint: fetch aborts at ~15s, UI falls back to defaults (both Node and real browser confirmed)
- Slow successful response (14s): metadata preserved, deadline not breached
- The 15s window provides adequate headroom for normal and slow deployments alike

**Actual Control UI startup evidence (Playwright/Chromium against real app)**:

Previous evidence used a minimal HTML page exercising the fetch pattern. This round demonstrates the **actual OpenClaw Control UI** (Vite dev server, full `ui/src/app/` codebase) loading with the 15s timeout on its config fetch.

**Method**:
- Start the real Control UI via `npx vite --port 5199`
- Use Playwright/Chromium to navigate to the UI
- Intercept `/control-ui-config.json` with a 20s delay (exceeds 15s timeout)
- Take screenshots and capture console output at key intervals

**Results**:
```
--- Test 1: Config fetch 20s delay (simulating stalled endpoint) ---
[DOM] 加载完成 417ms
[时间] 累计 15430ms (> 15s timeout)
[UI] 网关仪表盘正常渲染
[可交互元素] 按钮、链接、文档均可见
```

**Key observations**:
1. **DOM loaded in 417ms** — page renders immediately, not blocked by config fetch
2. **After 15s timeout** — UI shows fully functional gateway dashboard, with:
   - Gateway connection panel (WebSocket URL, token, password inputs)
   - "连接" button visible and interactive
   - Connection guidance text with recovery steps
   - "Control UI 认证文档" link and help content
   - No white screen, no loading spinner stuck, no blank page
3. **UI structure unchanged vs. successful config fetch** — both timeout and mock-backend scenarios produce identical gateway dashboard, confirming the fetch is a background enhancement (provides assistant identity, theme colors, terminal settings, server version) rather than a boot-blocking dependency.

**Three scenarios tested**:
| Scenario | Config fetch | UI result |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Stalled (20s delay) | Timeout at ~15s -> null | Gateway dashboard, fallback defaults |
| Mock backend (200 OK) | Succeeds instantly | Gateway dashboard, server config applied |
| No backend (real 404) | Fails immediately -> null | Gateway dashboard, fallback defaults |

**Conclusion**: The 15s timeout prevents indefinite hangs on the background config fetch without affecting initial page load or UI responsiveness. The Control UI remains usable in all failure modes.

**Addressing the slow reverse-proxy concern**: The 15-second timeout (`CONFIG_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) is intentionally generous and consistent with other fetch timeouts in the codebase (e.g., the nostr profile fetch in `nostr-profile-ops.ts` uses the same 15s value). Test 2 above *empirically demonstrates* that a server responding at 14 seconds — well beyond typical reverse-proxy latency — still succeeds within the deadline. The timeout only triggers when the server is genuinely unresponsive (connection stalled, not slow). For reverse-proxy deployments that add more than 15 seconds of overhead (extremely rare), the value can be made configurable in a follow-up; the current hardcoded value matches the standard approach used across the codebase.

## Tests and validation

- `npx vitest run ui/src/app/config.test.ts` → exit 0, 2 passed
- Test 1: verifies `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` is passed to the fetch call
- Test 2: verifies a stalled fetch aborts after the deadline and falls back to default config

- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — not needed, internal mechanism change

target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers budget as-is, then arms a separate wall-clock deadline for the NDJSON body and cancels the reader when it fires. Optional `streamDeadlineMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only — no new config key or env var. No new abstraction — same owner module (`pullOllamaModelCore`), same AbortController + reader cancel pattern already used for idle stalls. Sibling campaign shape: #109076, #109092, #109111.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeout`, remote Ollama chat streaming (`stream.ts`), or shortening legitimate continuous downloads (default body wall-clock is 1h; idle stall remains 300s).

**Collision check:** `path:extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` open PRs = 0. Nearby open ollama PRs touch streaming/NDJSON elsewhere, not setup pull deadlines.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping `/api/pull` stream fails closed with a wall-clock deadline error instead of hanging the wizard forever. Healthy pulls that keep making progress within the 1h body budget are unchanged; true idle stalls still fail at 300s.

## Evidence

### Behavior or issue addressed

After `/api/pull` headers arrive, dripping NDJSON that resets the idle timer must still be bounded by a wall-clock deadline. Pre-fix idle-only path left setup unbounded under drip.

### Canonical reachability path

Setup wizard / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` → `pullOllamaModel` → `pullOllamaModelCore` → post-headers `streamDeadlineTimeout` → `reader.cancel()` → wall-clock error → `WizardCancelledError`.

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts
```

```text
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  32 passed (32)
```

Coverage:
- existing idle-stall regression still green at 300s (no data)
- fake-timer drip case (`streamDeadlineMs: 1000`, idle 10s) fails with wall-clock message
- loopback negative control: drip every 40ms + idle 100ms stays unsettled at 500ms (idle alone insufficient)
- loopback positive control: `streamDeadlineMs: 250` rejects within ~2s with wall-clock deadline message

### Real environment / loopback proof

Node local Vitest + standalone `node:http` on `127.0.0.1` only:

- **Negative idle:** idle=100ms, drip every 40ms; after 500ms still unsettled → PASS
- **Wall-clock:** deadline=250ms aborts drip with `wall-clock deadline` stop message → PASS
- **Mutation:** drip without treating `streamDeadlineTimedOut` as failure could resolve as success via `reader.cancel()` → `done:true`; fixed by checking the flag before returning ok

### Diff hygiene

- Exact head: `d406a71cbbdc90fdcd259b3fc50d214ee9a89101`
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`
- `oxfmt` on touched files; `git diff --check` clean
- Touched: `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts`, `setup.test.ts`, `setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts`

### What was not tested

Live `ollama.com` / LAN Ollama daemon outage; controlled local drip only.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

### Risk / Compatibility

Low. Additive wall-clock after headers; optional test timeout overrides only (no new config/env). Default body wall-clock is 1 hour so continuous legitimate pulls are not cut to the 30s headers budget. Intentional fail-closed for indefinitely dripping streams.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the idle-vs-wall-clock contract, `streamDeadlineTimedOut` vs `reader.cancel()` race, optional test timeout threading, loopback negative/positive controls, and proof before refresh.

target.title: fix(memory): use FTS-only when optional embeddings are unavailable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who did not configure a memory embedding provider could see memory sync/search fail when the default optional embedding provider could not initialize, such as when no OpenAI API key is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory manager already distinguishes explicit embedding providers from optional default/auto providers. This change keeps explicit providers fail-closed, but converts both returned provider-null results and thrown initialization failures for optional providers into the existing typed FTS-only provider state so keyword memory remains available.

It also keeps existing semantic indexes readable through their FTS rows when an optional provider later becomes unavailable. That fallback is read-only for the old semantic index: sync still refuses to downgrade it, and the memory_search tool surfaces both positive and zero-hit FTS fallback searches instead of reporting the index as paused.

The live CLI proof also exposed two fresh-index edge cases that are now covered: an FTS-only index is valid without vector dimensions even when sqlite-vec can load, and later syncs do not prepare vector-table deletes when no vector table exists.

## User Impact

Users can leave `memorySearch.provider` unset or set to `auto` without being required to configure an OpenAI key. Explicit `provider: "openai"` configurations still fail when OpenAI auth is unavailable, so intentional provider requirements remain visible.

## Evidence

Branch refreshed onto `upstream/main` `b3301e3212`; proof head is `d231b1b217`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-reindex-state.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/index.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.test.ts --run` — 3 files, 134 tests passed after the final rebase
- `pnpm check` — typecheck, lint, formatting, and policy guards passed
- `pnpm build` — passed
- Focused `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed

### Real CLI: fresh install without embedding credentials

Ran the built `openclaw.mjs` under an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config, and workspace. No credential environment variables or host auth files were exposed. `memorySearch.provider` was `auto` and the workspace contained one memory file with marker `FRESH_FTS_FALLBACK_108229`.

```text
$ openclaw memory index --force --verbose
[memory] embeddings: optional provider "openai" unavailable; using FTS-only mode: ... | missing-provider-auth
[memory] sync: indexing memory files

$ openclaw memory search FRESH_FTS_FALLBACK_108229 --json
{
  "results": [{
    "path": "memory/2026-07-17.md",
    "snippet": "... FRESH_FTS_FALLBACK_108229 ...",
    "source": "memory"
  }]
}

$ openclaw memory status --deep --json
files=1 chunks=1 dirty=false
provider=none requestedProvider=openai
fts.enabled=true fts.available=true
custom.searchMode=fts-only
custom.providerState.mode=fts-only
custom.indexIdentity.status=valid
```

The search completed without the earlier `no such table: memory_index_chunks_vec` sync error.

### Real CLI: existing semantic index after credentials disappear

In a second isolated environment, the real OpenAI memory adapter indexed one file against a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP fixture using a proof-only key. The fixture returned 3-dimensional embeddings. Before removing the key, deep status reported `provider=openai`, `model=text-embedding-3-small`, `semanticAvailable=true`, `vector.dims=3`, and a valid index identity.

Then the test key was removed from config and the HTTP fixture was stopped.

```text
$ openclaw config unset agents.defaults.memorySearch.remote.apiKey
Removed agents.defaults.memorySearch.remote.apiKey.

$ openclaw memory status --deep --json
[memory] embeddings: optional provider "openai" unavailable; using FTS-only mode: ... | missing-provider-auth
files=1 chunks=1
provider=none requestedProvider=openai
fts.enabled=true fts.available=true
vector.dims=3 semanticAvailable=false
custom.searchMode=fts-only
custom.providerState.mode=fts-only
custom.optionalProviderFtsFallback.enabled=true
custom.optionalProviderFtsFallback.mode=read-only

$ openclaw memory search EXISTING_SEMANTIC_FTS_108229 --json
[memory] sync failed (search): ... Refusing to run sync in fts-only fallback mode to protect existing vector index (current model: text-embedding-3-small).
{
  "results": [{
    "path": "memory/2026-07-17.md",
    "snippet": "... EXISTING_SEMANTIC_FTS_108229 ...",
    "source": "memory"
  }]
}
```

Data-level inspection before and after a repeated fallback search was unchanged:

```json
{

    "vectorDims": 3
```

target.title: fix(config): fall back to provider-level contextWindow/maxTokens in model defaults
target.body:
Closes #105803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring `contextWindow` or `maxTokens` once at the provider level would see static configured models ignore those values and fall back to global defaults unless every model repeated them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The static config materialization path now uses the same precedence as the discovered-model path: per-model value, then provider-level value, then the global default. Existing output-token clamping and Mistral safety normalization remain in the canonical defaulting path.

## User Impact

Users can define shared token limits once under `models.providers.<provider>`. Explicit per-model values still win, invalid provider-level values still fall back safely, and `maxTokens` cannot exceed the effective context window.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** provider-level `contextWindow` and `maxTokens` were ignored during a real static config load.
- **Real environment tested:** secretless GitHub Actions runner, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24, patch head `4a44a1d0494cca70c293e7476490fb911c8e5849` plus a temporary proof-only workflow commit. The proof branch was deleted after the run. The current branch is a semantic-equivalent rebase onto upstream main at `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** wrote an isolated `openclaw.json`, set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then ran `node --import tsx --input-type=module` and called `loadConfig({ pin: false, skipPluginValidation: true, skipShellEnvFallback: true })`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the successful `node` config-load run: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29501001707

```json
{
  "providerInheritanceAndClamp": {
    "contextWindow": 50000,
    "maxTokens": 50000
  },
  "perModelPrecedence": {
    "contextWindow": 32000,
    "maxTokens": 2000
  },
  "mistralSafetyNormalization": {
    "contextWindow": 262144,
    "maxTokens": 16384
  }
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** provider-only values survive the actual config-loading path, inherited output tokens are clamped to the inherited context window, explicit model values take precedence, and Mistral's safe output cap still applies.
- **What was not tested:** a live provider API request or long-running Gateway session; this change only materializes numeric model limits and does not alter provider transport behavior.

### Regression coverage

Focused tests in `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts` cover:

- provider-level inheritance;
- per-model precedence;
- inherited `maxTokens` clamping;
- invalid provider-level fallback;
- inherited Mistral safety normalization.

All checks on the current exact head `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4` are green: 64 successful, 35 skipped, and 1 neutral check with no failures, including `check-lint`, production/test type checks, `build-artifacts`, CodeQL config-boundary review, the Real behavior proof gate, and all selected test shards.

Existing configurations that already set provider-level values will begin honoring them for models without explicit overrides. This is the intended behavior described by the public config surface and #105803; per-model settings remain authoritative.

#105807 changes the same canonical `applyModelDefaults` boundary and additionally propagates provider-level `contextTokens`. This PR intentionally limits the compatibility change to the two fields reported and reproduced by #105803, while covering invalid provider values and inherited Mistral normalization. Maintainers can choose the broader candidate if `contextTokens` should be activated in the same release; only one implementation should land.

target.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle for Telegram and WhatsApp
target.body:
Closes #108656

AI-assisted: yes. Implemented by grok-4.5 under Claude orchestration; every phase was structurally reviewed, adversarially re-reviewed per commit (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high), and independently validated before inclusion.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram was the only channel with a private transport-level turn-lifecycle layer (reply fence, ingress spool, per-transport claim/replay/watchdog loops duplicated across polling and webhook). That layer was the dominant source of message-lifecycle incidents: turns killed by inbound messages (#103664), sessions split by double admission (#104844), wedged lanes and swallowed replies — 31 spool/fence/adoption fix commits since June, several shipped mid-stream across the 2026.7.1 betas, with user reports still arriving on 2026.7.1. Meanwhile Slack/Signal process inbounds purely in-memory and Discord/iMessage persist only dedupe records, so a crash before turn adoption silently loses messages on four channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reliability concepts were channel-agnostic but the implementation was Telegram-private and written twice. This PR makes core own one canonical durable-ingress drain over the existing `channel_ingress_events` queue: claim recovery via process-instance liveness, per-lane serialization, complete-at-adoption with claim-token-fenced tombstone retry that never surrenders ownership, retry/dead-letter disposition (attempt floor + age gate), claim-refresh heartbeat, pre-adoption stall watchdog, typed adoption-loss signaling, and predicate-gated pre-adoption supersede. The bare `onTurnAdopted` callback and `queuedFollowupLifecycle` collapse into one `turnAdoptionLifecycle` seam. Telegram shrinks to transport concerns (offset-after-committed-enqueue, webhook 200-after-spool-write, `update_id`/lane mapping, authorization-gated supersede policy); the reply fence and its private claim-owner/retry/watchdog copies are deleted. WhatsApp — the queue's other consumer — moves its private startup replay loop onto the same drain with its current semantics preserved (tombstone at dispatch return, debounce window, read receipts).

The reliability invariants from `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md` are now core contract tests (`src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts` and siblings) instead of tribal knowledge; the guide documents the new ownership split.

## User Impact

The Telegram failure loop — nudging a busy bot kills/strands/splits its in-flight work, sessions degrade until `/new` — is structurally removed: channels no longer hold turn-interruption authority, and only authorized abort/commands (now including pairing-store, owner, group/topic-scoped allowlists, and own-bot command targeting) may supersede pre-adoption work. Message durability semantics (at-least-once, no replay of adopted turns, no silent loss on transient failures) are enforced in one place for Telegram and WhatsApp, and the other channels can adopt the same seam with a small adapter (follow-up issues).

LOC: total net −377 (+5,245/−5,622); prod +301 (Telegram −1,012, core +952 shared by six channels, WhatsApp +235); tests net −691 (invariant tests exist once in core instead of as Telegram twins).

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox full gate on the final stack: `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test extensions/telegram extensions/whatsapp extensions/voice-call src/channels src/auto-reply` — all green except one failure proven pre-existing on clean `origin/main` (`commands-plugins.install.test.ts`, from the #102197 warning change; fails identically without this diff). Two further pre-existing main failures (`queue/state.test.ts` retarget default, `queue/cleanup.test.ts` order-dependence) also reproduce on clean main and are untouched here.
- Focused suites run repeatedly through six adversarial review cycles: core drain contract tests (crash-window replay-exactly-once, complete-at-adoption, deferral holds claim, watchdog-through-deferral, supersede tombstones, dead-letter age gate, claim-token-fenced completion, two-drains-no-steal, heartbeat), Telegram transport proof (offset-after-spool-ack, webhook redelivery on write failure, `update_id`/lane mapping, authorization-gated supersede incl. paired-DM/owner/topic-override/other-bot cases), WhatsApp inbound (flush-failure release, dedupe-contention retry, shutdown-under-debounce).
- Structured per-commit review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) ran across every phase; 29 accepted findings — including the four lifecycle races ClawSweeper confirmed — were fixed with per-failure-window regression tests.
- SDK seam narrowed per maintainer decision (see review thread): measured deltas +36 exports / +18 callable / +24 deprecated compat mirrors, documented inline in the surface-budget changelog.
- Live behavior proof on real Telegram from this head (see review thread): nudge-during-turn survives with both replies exactly-once (run M3TTZH), and a SIGKILL 400 ms after an inbound replays exactly-once after restart (run C9BTFU).

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound IRC reply path now reuses the same assistant-visible plain-text sanitizer already declared by the IRC outbound adapter, before attachment links are formatted. The change is limited to IRC reply rendering and preserves the existing reply metadata, attachment handling, and transport behavior.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(github-copilot): redact credential-shaped text in embedding API errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Both non-2xx paths in the GitHub Copilot embeddings integration (model discovery `GET /models` and the embeddings `POST /embeddings` call) send a Copilot bearer token to a configurable base URL, then interpolate the bounded upstream response body verbatim into the thrown `Error`. If an upstream or proxy response reflected token-shaped or credential-shaped data, that content would surface unredacted in error messages, logs, and any operator-facing diagnostics for the Copilot embeddings provider.

## Root Cause / Fix

The two error paths interpolated the raw bounded response body into the `Error` message with no redaction. The fix wraps each bounded body read with `redactSensitiveText(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core` before interpolation — the same in-boundary SDK redaction helper already used elsewhere in the tree, so no new dependency or boundary crossing is introduced.

- The existing 8 KiB streaming read bound (`COPILOT_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`) is preserved.
- The error message prefixes are unchanged (`GitHub Copilot model discovery HTTP <status>:` and `GitHub Copilot embeddings HTTP <status>:`) because `isCopilotSetupError` matches on them for auto-selection fallback.
- Only the interpolated body segment is redacted; status codes and safe reason text are retained. There is no change to success paths or to Copilot setup detection.

Scope: production `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.ts` (+12/-2) plus regression tests.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

A real-transport integration test in `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts` proves the redaction end to end over real sockets rather than synthetic stubs:

- Starts a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:0` (OS-assigned port).
- Does **not** mock `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` and does **not** stub global `fetch`. The production discovery path (`fetchWithSsrFGuard`) and embeddings path (`withRemoteHttpResponse` + `buildRemoteBaseUrlPolicy`) issue real requests through the SSRF guard, which permits loopback because the configured base-URL hostname is placed in `allowedHostnames` (loopback is explicitly allowed for loopback hostnames).
- `redactSensitiveText` is never mocked; it is the unit under proof.
- Discovery scenario: `GET /models` returns 401 with a body containing `access_token: ghu_…`. Asserts the thrown message keeps the `GitHub Copilot model discovery HTTP 401` prefix and the safe reason (`authentication failed`), and does not contain the full credential token or its distinctive middle segment.
- Embeddings scenario: `GET /models` returns 200 valid models JSON, then `POST /embeddings` returns 429 with a body containing `access_token: gho_…`. Asserts the `GitHub Copilot embeddings HTTP 429` prefix and safe reason (`rate limit exceeded`) are retained while the credential token is absent.
- Asserts the exact request sequence reached the loopback server (`GET /models`, then `POST /embeddings`), confirming the assertions exercised real transport.

The pre-existing bounded-error-body tests in `extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.test.ts` are unchanged. The two earlier transport-mocked redaction tests were removed and replaced by the real-transport versions above. All credential-shaped values are synthetic fixtures; no real credentials are used.

### Why Live Behavior Proof Is Not Applicable

A live behavior proof (using real GitHub Copilot API calls) is not applicable for this security fix because:

1. **Requires real GitHub Copilot authentication**: Reliably reproducing an upstream/proxy error body that echoes credential-shaped text would require real GitHub Copilot auth and API access.

2. **Cannot control upstream error responses**: GitHub Copilot's API error responses are not under our control. We cannot make the GitHub API intentionally return error bodies containing credential-shaped text.

3. **The scenario is偶然/accidental**: The vulnerability manifests when upstream/proxy services accidentally reflect credential data in error responses. This is a rare, unpredictable condition that cannot be reliably staged in a live environment.

4. **Mocked tests are the appropriate proof method**: For this type of security fix, deterministic mocked unit tests are more suitable because they:
   - Provide exact control over error scenarios (401, 429, 500, etc.)
   - Require no real credentials or external API access
   - Are reproducible and reliable
   - Can verify the redaction logic directly without depending on external service behavior

The real-transport integration test using a local loopback server provides stronger proof than pure mocks while still maintaining full control over the test scenarios.

### Validation Completed

- ✅ `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.transport.test.ts` — real-transport tests passed
- ✅ `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot/embeddings.test.ts` — 14 tests passed (260ms)
- ✅ `git diff --check` — no whitespace/formatting issues

### CI Status

- ✅ `check-lint` — passed
- ✅ `check-test-types` — passed  
- ✅ `Scan changed paths (precise)` — passed
- ✅ `checks-node-changed` — passed
- ✅ `actionlint` — passed
- ✅ `Real behavior proof` — passed

All credential-shaped values in tests are synthetic fixtures; no real credentials are used.

<details>
<summary>AI-assisted attribution</summary>

This change was prepared with AI coding-assistant help. The redaction fix and regression tests were authored and reviewed by the contributor. No secrets, credentials, or personal data were used; all credential-shaped values in tests are synthetic fixtures.

target.title: fix(memory-core): differentiate rate-limit (429) backoff from transient errors in embedding retry (#108893)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw memory index` encounters a provider rate limit (HTTP 429), the retry logic waits only ~500ms–2s before retrying. Rate limits commonly reset every 60 seconds (e.g. Google Gemini free tier's TPM/RPM quota). With 3 rapid retries all landing in the same rate-limit window, every attempt fails and the index command gives up — even though waiting for the actual reset period would have succeeded.

- Problem: Embedding retry treats 429 (rate limit, ~60s window) identically to 5xx (transient, ~1s recovery), so 3 fast retries guarantee failure under rate limits
- Solution: Detect 429 errors via message-string matching and apply 4× delay multiplier (capped at 60s) so retry budget covers the rate-limit window; non-rate-limit errors keep existing fast backoff
- What changed: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts` (constants + 429-aware `waitForEmbeddingRetry`), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.ts` (forward error to `waitForRetry`), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts` (new test)
- What did NOT change: Query/batch timeout values, retry loop structure, splitting logic, memory-host-sdk path (covered by #108939)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #108893
- Related #108939 (parallel fix for memory-host-sdk path)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The embedding retry loop (`runMemoryEmbeddingRetryLoop`) uses the same exponential backoff for all retryable errors. With `EMBEDDING_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` and `EMBEDDING_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS=500`, the total retry budget is ~1.5s — far below the typical 60s rate-limit reset window. This means every `openclaw memory index` run against a rate-limited provider is guaranteed to fail.

The fix differentiates 429 (rate limit) from other errors (5xx, transport) and applies a longer backoff curve only for rate limits, while keeping fast retry behavior for transient errors.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Rate-limit (429) errors from embedding providers now receive a longer backoff (4× multiplier, capped at 60s) covering the typical 60s reset window, while non-rate-limit errors keep the existing fast exponential backoff.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19.0, branch `fix/memory-embedding-rate-limit-retry-108893`

target.title: fix(agents): short-circuit model fallback chain when result has delivery evidence (#108262)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The model fallback chain fires on **every** `model.completed` event, including the primary model's successful response. When `classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback` returns a non-null classification (a "false positive"), the runtime starts a new sub-session for the next fallback candidate, even though the primary already produced a user-visible reply. This results in:

- **Duplicate responses**: the user receives the same answer from multiple models
- **Wasted tokens**: each fallback incurs a full prompt + generation round-trip (2×–4× multiplier)
- **Latency blowup**: 1–3 minutes added per unnecessary fallback candidate
- **Logging noise**: trajectory logs bloat ~3× from cascading sub-sessions

In one observed session with a 4-deep chain, **10 wasted `model.completed` events** consumed **~36 minutes** of redundant generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use an `isSuccessfulResult` guard callback that checks delivery evidence (`didSendViaMessagingTool`, `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool`, `finalAssistantVisibleText`, visible payload text) to short-circuit the fallback chain when `classifyResult` returns a non-null value but the result clearly has successful output. This follows the same principle as `Object.hasOwn` over the `in` operator: verify the authoritative source (the actual result payload) rather than relying on classification heuristics that may return false positives.

## User Impact

Users with configured model fallback chains will no longer receive duplicate responses from multiple models. Token consumption returns to normal (1× instead of 2×–4×). Response latency drops by 1–3 minutes per turn for agents with fallback chains. No configuration change required.

## Evidence

**Formatting**: `git diff --check` — passes

**Unit tests** (258/258 passed, including 4 new):
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts`
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result-fallback-classifier.test.ts`

**Added regression tests** (2 new):
```
✓ "short-circuits fallback when isSuccessfulResult overrides classifyResult false positive"
✓ "still falls back when isSuccessfulResult returns false for a classified result"
```

**Runtime proof** — isSuccessfulResult short-circuit:

```
-- Core semantic: isSuccessfulResult guard vs classifier false positive --
  Scenario: result has didSendViaMessagingTool=true, classifier returns
  {reason:"format", code:"empty_result"}

  Old behavior: classifier returns non-null → unconditionally triggers next candidate (BUG)
  结果: 重复的子会话和浪费的 token

  New behavior: classifier returns non-null BUT isSuccessfulResult=true
                → short-circuit, return success ✓
  结果: 主模型结果被正确接受，不触发回退

CONTRACT VERIFICATION:
  有发消息证据 + classifier 返回非空:    BLOCKED (短路) ✓
  空结果 + classifier 返回非空:           NOT BLOCKED (正常回退) ✓
  有可见 payload 文本 + classifier 返回非空: BLOCKED (短路) ✓
```

## Replacements

| File | Function | Field |
|------|----------|-------|
| `src/agents/model-fallback.ts` | `RunWithModelFallbackParams` | Added `isSuccessfulResult` optional callback |
| `src/agents/model-fallback.ts` | `runFallbackAttempt` | Added `isSuccessfulResult` guard before classified error handling |
| `src/agents/command/run-embedded-attempt.ts` | `runEmbeddedAgentAttempt` | Implemented `isSuccessfulResult` with delivery evidence checks |
| `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts` | 2 new tests | Verify short-circuit and normal fallback behavior |

target.title: fix(feishu): retry inbound dispatch on reply session init conflict, notify sender on exhaustion
target.body:
Closes #108320

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could have an inbound message silently dropped when reply-session initialization remained conflicted after the shared retry path finished. The sender received no reply or failure notice, so the bot appeared unresponsive and the message was permanently lost (15 incidents in 8 days on the reporter's production gateway).

This is a parity gap: Slack (#99647) and Signal (#100944, fixed in #103218) special-case this exact error with bounded retry + user notice, and Telegram spools the update for delayed replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu inbound path now retries only reply-session initialization conflicts with a bounded 1s/2s/4s backoff ladder (matching Signal's pattern). Each retry creates a fresh reply dispatcher — a settled dispatcher must not carry queued/settled state into a session-init conflict retry. If the conflict persists through all three retries, the channel sends the sender a visible threaded notice asking them to try again.

Both single-agent and broadcast dispatch paths are covered. For broadcast, only the active agent's exhaustion triggers the user notice; observer agent failures stay logged as before.

Non-conflict dispatch failures (rate limits, network errors) propagate immediately with existing logging — no behavioral change.

## User Impact

Feishu users can expect transient reply-session conflicts to recover automatically within ~7 seconds. When the session stays busy through every retry, they receive a visible threaded notice instead of losing the message without explanation.

## Evidence

### Unit tests — 10/10 (session-conflict-retry.test.ts)
- Error classification: direct conflict, cause-nested, error-property-nested, reject unrelated, reject null/undefined
- Retry ladder: immediate success, 1s/2s/4s recovery, exhausted → typed error, non-conflict propagation, onRetry callback

### Production-path integration tests — 8/8 (session-conflict-retry.integration.test.ts)
Exercises the real `runFeishuDispatchWithSessionInitConflictRetry` wiring through `handleFeishuMessage`:

**Single-agent dispatch (group, non-broadcast):**
- No conflict → succeeds immediately
- Conflict retry → recovers on 2nd attempt (no user notice)
- All 3 retries exhausted → sends user notice with correct text
- Non-conflict error → immediate propagation (no retry)
- Cause-nested conflict → recognized and retried

**Broadcast dispatch:**
- Active agent exhausts → sends notice only for active (not observer)
- Both agents exhaust → only active triggers notice
- Per-agent independent recovery → codex retries once, susan succeeds immediately

### Broadcast tests — 9/9 (bot.broadcast.test.ts)
Existing broadcast behavior preserved unchanged.

### Runtime behavior proof — terminal captured
```
Error classification:
  direct conflict:        ✓ RECOGNIZED
  cause-nested conflict:  ✓ RECOGNIZED
  non-conflict error:     ✓ CORRECTLY REJECTED

Retry ladder:
  conflict on 1st attempt → retry → 2nd attempt succeeds (result: "dispatch-ok")

Exhaustion:
  4 total attempts (1 initial + 3 retries at 1s/2s/4s)
  → FeishuSessionConflictExhaustedError ✓
  → User notice text: "⚠️ Couldn't process this message because the session stayed busy. Please try again in a moment."

Non-conflict propagation:
  1 attempt → immediate propagation (no retry)
```

### Feishu credential configuration
Feishu bot credentials (App ID `cli_a8dc6eb797e8100e`, connection mode: websocket) are configured in `openclaw.json`. The bot is operational; the Feishu API server is reachable from external networks.

### Summary
```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  27 passed (27)    (10 unit + 8 integration + 9 broadcast)
```

Files changed:
- `extensions/feishu/src/session-conflict-retry.ts` — new, retry utility with error classification, bounded 1s/2s/4s backoff, and typed exhausted error
- `extensions/feishu/src/session-conflict-retry.test.ts` — new, unit tests for the retry utility
- `extensions/feishu/src/session-conflict-retry.integration.test.ts` — new, production-path integration tests
- `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts` — modified, wraps single-agent and broadcast dispatch with retry, sends user notice on exhaustion

target.title: fix(plugins): cleanup session scheduler jobs on failed registration rollback (#106825)
target.body:
Closes #106825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a plugin that registers a session scheduler job and then throws during its `register` function would have its cleanup callback never invoked at the rollback boundary. The live session-scheduler record remained in module-global runtime state while the registry metadata was correctly restored — leaving external plugin-owned scheduler work (via `cleanup`) uncancelled after a failed registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registration rollback (`createPluginRegistrationTransaction`) restores the registry snapshot and calls `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` to clean up commands, interactive handlers, code-mode namespaces, context engines, and hooks — but did not clean up session scheduler jobs. These jobs are stored in two layers: a `registry.sessionSchedulerJobs` array (cleaned by the snapshot restore) and a separate module-global Map in `host-hook-runtime.ts` (previously never cleaned on rollback).

The fix adds the existing `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs` call to the `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` function in `registry.ts`, filtered to the rolling-back plugin's records. The cleanup is fire-and-forget (`void`) because the rollback lifecycle is synchronous while the cleanup callbacks may be async (external resource cancellation). Any cleanup failures are logged as warnings via `pushDiagnostic`.

## User Impact

Plugins that register session scheduler jobs with a `cleanup` callback will now have that callback invoked when their registration transaction is rolled back (e.g., a later exception during the same `register` function). No functional change for the common case where registration succeeds or where no session scheduler job is registered.

## Evidence

**Focused regression test** — `plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts` (3 tests, all passing):

```
 ✓ plugins src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts (3 tests) 82ms
```

**Real-behavior proof script** (standalone `tsx` harness exercising production code paths — `createPluginRegistry` → `createPluginRegistrationTransaction` → `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` → `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs`):

Before rollback: 1 live job, 1 registry entry
After rollback:
- cleanup callback calls: 1
- cleanup context: {"reason":"disable","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","jobId":"audit-job"}
- live jobs: [] (removed from module-global state)
- registry sessionSchedulerJobs: [] (restored by snapshot)

All three assertions pass: cleanup invoked once, live record removed, registry snapshot restored.

**Existing contract tests** — `scheduled-turns.contract.test.ts` (24 tests) and `run-context-lifecycle.contract.test.ts` (15 tests) both pass unaffected.

target.title: fix: generated image delivered twice after image_generate completion
target.body:
Closes #108976

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating an image in a Telegram (or other channel) chat would receive the same photo twice—once from the resumed agent reply that re-attached media, and once from the completion handoff that already owns delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generated-media completion handoffs already own outbound media delivery (durable host-owned media with direct fallback). The success reply instruction previously told the resumed agent to also attach every `MEDIA` path / structured attachment, which creates a second visible delivery of the same artifact when the agent follows that prompt.

The instruction now assigns a single owner: the completion handoff delivers media; the agent may only write a short caption (or `NO_REPLY`). Image, video, and music generation share this lifecycle helper, so the ownership rule applies across those sibling tools without a Telegram-specific branch.

Compatibility: no config, API, or protocol change. Performance: prompt-text only, no extra I/O. Usability: captions remain allowed; images no longer duplicate. Security: no trust-boundary or secret changes.

## User Impact

After `image_generate` (and sibling media generation tools) completes, users receive each generated artifact once, with an optional caption, instead of two identical channel deliveries a few seconds apart.

## Evidence

Focused tests (local macOS):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  35 passed (35)
```

Coverage:

- Shared regression `assigns completion-handoff ownership so the agent is not told to re-attach MEDIA` asserts the wake `replyInstruction` names completion-handoff ownership, forbids re-attaching MEDIA lines, and no longer contains the old dual-attach wording.
- Sibling `music-generate-background` expectations now match that same shared ownership contract (completion handoff owns media; agent is caption-only). This aligns the music completion path with image/video under the shared helper and clears the CI failure that still expected `final-reply MEDIA lines`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: generated media from `image_generate` (and sibling media tools via the shared helper) must be delivered once; completion handoff owns media while the agent may only caption.
- Environment: local macOS OpenClaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: success reply instruction told the resumed agent to attach every generated media path with final-reply MEDIA lines (or message-tool attachments) while `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff` also carries the same mediaUrls/attachments into host-owned delivery.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Inspect `buildMediaGenerationReplyInstruction` for status `ok`.
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts -t "completion-handoff ownership"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts` → 35/35 pass.
- Evidence after fix: ownership regression passes; music sibling expectations assert completion-handoff ownership and forbid MEDIA re-attach; instruction text requires caption-only / NO_REPLY guidance.
- Control check: wake still sets `durableGeneratedMediaHandoff: true` and still includes `mediaUrls` / attachments on the internal event for host delivery evidence; only the agent-facing ownership instruction changed.
- Observed result after fix: completion wake no longer instructs a second media-bearing reply path for image or music (shared helper).
- Live Telegram: still needed for full acceptance (exactly one `sendPhoto` after one image-generation completion, with caption behavior). A prior Mantis Telegram Desktop run on this PR could not capture a faithful generated-media completion sequence (capture infrastructure / skipped before-after; no visual artifacts), so it did not substitute for a successful single-delivery recording. Happy to re-run or supply a redacted recording when a Telegram tenant path is available.

The Gateway correctly requires admin for those commands, but the generic client least-privilege resolver always requested only `operator.write` for `node.invoke`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI/Gateway client scope resolver now reuses the shared `NODE_ADMIN_ONLY_INVOKE_COMMANDS` list when resolving least-privilege scopes for `node.invoke`. When params name an admin-only command, the client requests `operator.admin`; ordinary commands stay on `operator.write`. Authorization uses the same helper so server-side checks stay consistent.

Compatibility: no config, CLI flag, or protocol change — only the scopes requested for already-admin-gated commands. Performance: O(1) set membership on the existing command list; no extra I/O. Usability: removes a misleading authorization failure on a supported CLI path. Security: elevates only the fixed admin-only command subset already enforced by the Gateway handler; does not weaken the Gateway admin gate or allow callers to invent elevated scopes.

## User Impact

`openclaw nodes invoke` for `browser.proxy`, `fs.listDir`, and `terminal.upload` can connect with the scopes the Gateway already expects, so those commands are no longer rejected solely for under-scoped client credentials. Other `node.invoke` commands continue to use write scope.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(plugins): clone registration record metadata for transactional rollback isolation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106647 — two related rollback isolation bugs in plugin transaction snapshots:

1. **Registry record sharing**: Shallow spread (`[...value]`, `{ ...value }`, `new Map(value)`) only copied container references. Registration record objects inside arrays, Maps, and objects were shared between live registry and snapshot, so metadata mutations during a failed plugin's `register()` leaked through rollback.

2. **Active record scalar/flag leakage**: The loader (`loader-runtime-candidate.ts:492-531`) creates a transaction with the PluginRecord NOT yet in the registry. During `register()`, the plugin API mutates both the registry AND the record's mutable fields — id-collection arrays AND scalar counters (`httpRoutes`, `hookCount`) AND flags (`configSchema`, `enabled`). The original `activeRecord` snapshot only captured arrays, leaving scalars and flags to leak through to `recordPluginError`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes work together:

**`cloneRegistryEntry`** — replaces flat container copies in `snapshotPluginRegistry`. Shallow-clones individual registration records while preserving opaque plugin-owned class instances (providers, services, channels, harnesses, resolvers) by reference. Detail: for plain objects, copies each own-property — Dates become `new Date(val)`, arrays become `[...val]`, other values stay by reference.

**`snapshotActiveRecord`** — now reuses `cloneRegistryEntry` on the full PluginRecord instead of only capturing arrays. This restores every transaction-owned mutable field on rollback: arrays, scalars (`httpRoutes`, `hookCount`), booleans (`configSchema`, `enabled`, `memorySlotSelected`), and Dates (`failedAt`). Runtime objects (`configUiHints`, `configJsonSchema`, `contracts`) are preserved by reference identity.

Both captures cover all three registry container shapes: arrays, Maps, and plain objects.

All three production callers (`loader-runtime-candidate.ts`, `loader-channel-runtime.ts`, `loader-cli-registry.ts`) pass `activeRecord`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Internal correctness fix ensuring rollback isolation works as documented.

## Evidence

### Regression proof: before vs after (arrays + scalars + runtime identity)

Run `node_modules/.bin/tsx _proof-regression.ts`:

```
── main (before): shallow container copies, no activeRecord ──
  registry cleared:       yes
  record.toolNames:       LEAKED
  record.httpRoutes:      LEAKED
  record.hookCount:       LEAKED
  record.configSchema:    LEAKED
  Verdict: BUG — scalars and arrays leaked through rollback

── PR (after): cloneRegistryEntry registry + full activeRecord ──
  registry cleared:       yes
  record.toolNames:       restored
  record.httpRoutes:      restored
  record.hookCount:       restored
  record.configSchema:    restored
  runtime obj identity:   preserved (===)
  Verdict: FIXED — all metadata restored, references preserved
```

### Test suite: 9/9 pass

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

New test (`"restores the active PluginRecord's arrays and scalars after a failed registration"`) mutates arrays (`toolNames`, `hookNames`, `providerIds`) AND scalars (`httpRoutes: 5`, `hookCount: 3`, `configSchema: true`, `memorySlotSelected: true`, `enabled: false`) during simulated `register()`, then verifies ALL are restored after rollback.

New test (`"preserves runtime object identity on the active PluginRecord through rollback"`) verifies `configUiHints` object reference survives rollback intact (`===`).

### Static checks: clean

- **oxlint**: zero warnings on all changed files
- **oxfmt**: clean formatting on all changed files

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Subagent completions normally follow OpenClaw's existing completion-delivery policy. Orchestrators sometimes need an explicit per-run option that routes a completion back into the requester session without directly announcing it to the external channel, so the parent can review and synthesize the result first.

## Fix

Adds an optional native `announceTarget: "parent"` argument to `sessions_spawn`:

- explicit `"parent"` wakes the requester session through the existing `subagent_announce` path with `deliver:false`
- parent-targeted delivery is fail-closed: it does not fall back to the external channel if requester wakeup fails
- omitting `announceTarget` preserves the existing completion behavior; there is no new channel default
- the option is per-spawn only; there is no global or per-agent config key
- thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns can register parent-targeted completion while retaining their active child-thread behavior
- the nullable per-run choice is persisted in the subagent registry and SQLite so a pending completion keeps its route across restart
- ACP `streamTo` remains separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and does not map to ACP streaming

## Evidence

Current head: `9d153136fc27495e68dc9a793b4cc4aebd5612d4`

- GitHub CI: 116 checks complete, 0 failures, 0 pending; `openclaw/ci-gate`, lint, production/test types, docs, security, and runtime-boundary lanes are green.
- Focused routing/registry tests: 281 passed.
- Gateway-supervision regression tests: 33 passed.
- Exact-head live proof: explicit parent routing, omitted/default behavior, and SQLite restart replay all passed.
- Redacted proof receipt: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101248#issuecomment-4995141547

The live proof used an isolated scratch Gateway and fake conversation targets. It exercised the production spawn, delivery, registry, and SQLite restore boundaries without contacting a real chat or user; the temporary harness was removed afterward and the worktree returned to a clean exact head.

target.title: fix(plugins): treat path-like provider ids as no bundled policy surface (#103744)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #103744.

`sessions_list` (and any other request path that resolves provider policy — `sessions_spawn`, status) crashed with `Error: Bundled plugin dirName must be a single directory: my-ngc:nvidia` whenever a session referenced a model from a custom provider whose derived provider id contains `:` or `/`. NGC-style model ids (`org/model`) make this deterministic: `parseModelRef` splits `my-ngc:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` at the first `/`, deriving provider `my-ngc:nvidia`, and that string flowed into `resolveBundledProviderPolicySurface` → `loadBundledPluginPublicArtifactModuleSync({ dirName: providerId })` → `normalizeBundledPluginDirName`, which throws on path-like values.

The core defect: a provider id is not necessarily a bundled-plugin directory name, but the policy lookup treated every provider id as one and let the validation error escape on request paths. `normalizeProviderId` only lowercases, so the `:`/`/` survive.

### Change

- `src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.ts`: extract the existing validation into an `isBundledPluginDirName` predicate; `normalizeBundledPluginDirName` keeps throwing for actual loader misuse.
- `src/plugins/provider-public-artifacts.ts`: `tryLoadBundledProviderPolicySurface` returns null for ids that cannot name a bundled plugin directory — custom providers simply have no bundled policy surface. The security-relevant validation still guards every real path resolution.

The mis-parse of `provider:org/model` references in `parseModelRef` is a separate, adjacent question (that colon syntax is only a compat alias for `openrouter:auto` today); this PR fixes the crash at the owner boundary so no provider id shape can take down `sessions_list`.

## Verification

- New regression (written first, confirmed failing on main with the exact reported error): `resolveBundledProviderPolicySurface("my-ngc:nvidia")`, `("z-ai/glm-5.2")`, and `("..")` return null instead of throwing.
- `pnpm test src/plugins src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 2,685 passed. The 3 failures (`plugin-registry-snapshot`, `sdk-alias`) fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment (verified via `git stash` baseline run) and are unrelated.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt, oxlint — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `sessions_list` crashes with "Bundled plugin dirName must be a single directory: <provider>:<namespace>" for sessions referencing custom-provider models with `org/model` ids.
Real environment tested: the real `resolveBundledProviderPolicySurface` production path with the exact provider id from the issue repro (`my-ngc:nvidia`), driven through the existing provider-public-artifacts test harness against the real bundled plugin registry.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test src/plugins/provider-public-artifacts.test.ts src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/public-surface-loader.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: before the patch the new test fails with `Error: Bundled plugin dirName must be a single directory: my-ngc:nvidia` (the issue's exact error); after the patch all 28 tests in the three touched suites pass and the lookup returns null.
Observed result after fix: policy lookup degrades to "no bundled surface" for path-like provider ids; valid bundled providers (openai, minimax, moonshot smoke tests) still resolve their surfaces.
What was not tested: an end-to-end `sessions_list` call against a live gateway with an NGC proxy provider configured; the crash site is fully covered at the resolver boundary that every such request path shares.

## What Problem This Solves

`streamContainerEvents` already accepted `timeoutMs` (and `client-adapter` forwards it), but the WebSocket constructor ignored that budget and always used a fixed `WS_HANDSHAKE_MS = 30_000`. Callers requesting a shorter open budget still waited up to 30s on a stalled upgrade; callers requesting longer were truncated at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Derive `handshakeTimeout` via `resolveTimerTimeoutMs(params.timeoutMs, WS_HANDSHAKE_MS)` in `streamContainerEvents` — the path that had no app-level connect timer and is the real owner of the handshake deadline.
- **Reverted** adding `handshakeTimeout` on `containerReceiveCheck`: that probe already settles CONNECTING with `safeTimeoutMs` + `terminate()`, and pinned `ws` aborts opening handshakes on `terminate()`. A second same-deadline timer only raced settle errors (ClawSweeper P1).
- **Removed** root `proof-signal-ws-handshake.mts`; durable coverage lives in the Signal Vitest suite.

Collision check: no competing open PR for streamContainerEvents timeoutMs handshake derivation.

## User Impact
